topics.title: Binary Operations and Cayley Tables
topics.short: A binary operation combines two elements of a set into one element of the set; a Cayley table lists every product a ∗ b (row a, column b), so you can read off closure, an identity and commutativity.

topics.title: The Group Axioms
topics.short: A group is a set with an associative operation, an identity and an inverse for every element; decide which axiom fails for examples like ℤ under subtraction or ℤₙ under multiplication.

topics.title: The Groups ℤₙ and U(n)
topics.short: ℤₙ is {0, 1, …, n − 1} under addition mod n; U(n) is the set of residues coprime to n under multiplication mod n, a group of order φ(n).

topics.title: First Proofs: Uniqueness, Cancellation and Inverses
topics.short: From the axioms alone: the identity and inverses are unique, ab = ac gives b = c, and (ab)⁻¹ = b⁻¹a⁻¹.

topics.title: The Order of an Element
topics.short: The order of a is the least n ≥ 1 with aⁿ = e (n·a = 0 when the operation is addition), and aᵏ = e exactly when the order of a divides k.

topics.title: Subgroups and the Subgroup Test
topics.short: H is a subgroup when it is a group under the same operation; it is enough that H is nonempty and ab⁻¹ ∈ H for all a, b ∈ H (for a finite H, closure alone is enough).

topics.title: Cyclic Groups and Generators
topics.short: ⟨a⟩ = {aᵏ : k ∈ ℤ} is the smallest subgroup containing a; G is cyclic when one element generates it, and k generates ℤₙ exactly when gcd(k, n) = 1.

topics.title: Orders of Powers
topics.short: If a has order n, then aᵏ has order n / gcd(n, k); in ℤₙ the element k has order n / gcd(n, k).

topics.title: Subgroups of Cyclic Groups
topics.short: Every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic; ℤₙ has exactly one subgroup of each order d dividing n, namely ⟨n/d⟩, and it has φ(d) elements of order d.

topics.title: Subgroup Lattices
topics.short: Draw the subgroups of a group ordered by inclusion; for ℤₙ the picture is the divisor diagram of n turned upside down, and you read off intersections and joins.

topics.title: Permutations and Composition
topics.short: A permutation is a bijection from {1, …, n} to itself; Sₙ is the group of all n! of them under composition, and στ means do τ first, then σ.

topics.title: Cycle Notation
topics.short: Follow 1 → σ(1) → σ(σ(1)) → … until you come back, then start a new cycle with the smallest unused number; disjoint cycles commute, and overlapping cycles must be multiplied out.

topics.title: The Order of a Permutation
topics.short: Write σ as disjoint cycles: its order is the lcm of the cycle lengths, and its cycle type tells how many permutations share its shape.

topics.title: Even and Odd Permutations
topics.short: Every permutation is a product of transpositions, always an even number or always an odd number of them; a k-cycle is even when k is odd, and the even permutations form Aₙ, of order n!/2.

topics.title: Dihedral Groups
topics.short: Dₙ is the group of the 2n symmetries of a regular n-gon: rotations rᵏ and reflections rᵏs, with rⁿ = s² = e and sr = r⁻¹s.

topics.title: Cosets
topics.short: The left coset aH = {ah : h ∈ H}; the left cosets of H all have |H| elements and split G into disjoint pieces, and aH = bH exactly when a⁻¹b ∈ H.

topics.title: Lagrange's Theorem
topics.short: If H is a subgroup of a finite group G, then |H| divides |G|, and the index [G : H] = |G|/|H| counts the cosets.

topics.title: Consequences of Lagrange's Theorem
topics.short: The order of every element divides |G|, so a^|G| = e; a group of prime order is cyclic; and Fermat's and Euler's theorems follow by taking G = U(n).

topics.title: Normal Subgroups
topics.short: N is normal when gNg⁻¹ = N for every g, which is the same as gN = Ng; subgroups of abelian groups and subgroups of index 2 are always normal.

topics.title: Quotient Groups
topics.short: When N is normal, the cosets of N form a group G/N with (aN)(bN) = abN, of order |G|/|N|.

topics.title: Group Homomorphisms
topics.short: φ : G → H is a homomorphism when φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b); then φ(e) = e, φ(a⁻¹) = φ(a)⁻¹, and the order of φ(a) divides the order of a.

topics.title: Kernels and Images
topics.short: The kernel {g : φ(g) = e} is a normal subgroup, the image is a subgroup, φ is one-to-one exactly when the kernel is {e}, and |G| = |ker φ| · |im φ|.

topics.title: Isomorphic Groups
topics.short: An isomorphism is a bijective homomorphism; to show two groups are not isomorphic, find a property one has and the other lacks: order, being abelian or cyclic, or how many elements have each order.

topics.title: Cayley's Theorem
topics.short: Every group is isomorphic to a group of permutations: g acts on G by x ↦ gx, so a group of order n sits inside Sₙ.

topics.title: The First Isomorphism Theorem
topics.short: If φ : G → H is a homomorphism, then G/ker φ ≅ im φ; use it to name quotients such as ℤ/nℤ ≅ ℤₙ and Sₙ/Aₙ ≅ ℤ₂.

topics.title: Direct Products
topics.short: In G × H the operation works coordinate by coordinate; the order of (g, h) is lcm(|g|, |h|), and ℤₘ × ℤₙ ≅ ℤₘₙ exactly when gcd(m, n) = 1.

topics.title: Classifying Finite Abelian Groups
topics.short: Every finite abelian group is a product of cyclic groups of prime-power order; for order pᵃ the choices match the partitions of a, so you can list them all.

topics.title: Invariant Factors and Telling Abelian Groups Apart
topics.short: Regroup a product of cyclic groups so each order divides the next (ℤ₂ × ℤ₄ × ℤ₃ ≅ ℤ₂ × ℤ₁₂), and count elements of each order to tell abelian groups apart.

topics.title: Group Actions
topics.short: A group acts on a set X when each g moves points, x ↦ g·x, with e·x = x and g·(h·x) = (gh)·x; the orbit of x is everywhere it can go, and its stabilizer is the subgroup that fixes it.

topics.title: The Orbit–Stabilizer Theorem
topics.short: For a finite group, |orbit of x| · |stabilizer of x| = |G|, because the points of the orbit match the cosets of the stabilizer.

topics.title: Conjugacy Classes and the Class Equation
topics.short: Conjugacy classes are the orbits of G acting on itself by x ↦ gxg⁻¹; in Sₙ they are the cycle types, and |G| = |Z(G)| + the sum of [G : C(x)] over the classes with more than one element.

topics.title: Burnside's Lemma
topics.short: The number of orbits is the average number of points fixed by a group element; count necklaces and colorings up to symmetry by adding up the fixed colorings over the group.

topics.title: The Sylow Theorems
topics.short: If |G| = pᵃm with p not dividing m, then G has subgroups of order pᵃ, they are all conjugate, and their number nₚ divides m and is ≡ 1 (mod p).

topics.title: Rings
topics.short: A ring is an abelian group under addition with an associative multiplication that distributes over it; ℤ, ℤₙ, matrices and polynomials are rings, and the units are the elements with multiplicative inverses.

topics.title: Integral Domains and Fields
topics.short: A zero divisor is an a ≠ 0 with ab = 0 for some b ≠ 0; an integral domain has none, every field is one, and ℤₙ is a field exactly when n is prime.

topics.title: Ideals
topics.short: An ideal is an additive subgroup I with ra and ar in I for every r in R and a in I; nℤ and ⟨d⟩ in ℤₙ are ideals, and every ideal of ℤ has the form nℤ.

topics.title: Ring Homomorphisms
topics.short: φ respects both operations, φ(a + b) = φ(a) + φ(b) and φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b); its kernel is an ideal, and reduction ℤ → ℤₙ and evaluation f ↦ f(c) are the key examples.

topics.title: Quotient Rings
topics.short: For an ideal I, the cosets a + I form a ring R/I; compute in ℝ[x]/(x² + 1), where x² can be replaced by −1, and in ℤₚ[x]/(f) by taking remainders.

topics.title: Prime and Maximal Ideals
topics.short: P is prime when ab ∈ P forces a ∈ P or b ∈ P, and M is maximal when no ideal lies strictly between M and R; R/P is an integral domain and R/M is a field.

topics.title: Polynomial Rings
topics.short: R[x] holds the polynomials with coefficients in R; over an integral domain deg(fg) = deg f + deg g, but in ℤₙ[x] with n composite degrees can drop.

topics.title: Division and Roots in F[x]
topics.short: Over a field, f = qg + r with deg r < deg g; c is a root of f exactly when x − c divides f, so a nonzero polynomial of degree n has at most n roots.

topics.title: The Euclidean Algorithm for Polynomials
topics.short: Repeated division finds gcd(f, g) in F[x], and running it backward writes the gcd as af + bg, which is how inverses are found in F[x]/(p(x)).

topics.title: Irreducible Polynomials of Degree 2 and 3
topics.short: A polynomial of degree 2 or 3 over a field is irreducible exactly when it has no root in the field, so over ℤₚ you can test every element.

topics.title: Testing Irreducibility over ℚ
topics.short: Use the rational root test, Gauss's lemma, Eisenstein's criterion (a prime dividing every coefficient but the leading one, with p² not dividing the constant) and reduction mod p.

topics.title: Field Extensions
topics.short: If p(x) is irreducible over F, then F[x]/(p(x)) is a field containing a root of p; ℚ(√2) = {a + b√2 : a, b ∈ ℚ} is one, with inverses found by the conjugate.

topics.title: Minimal Polynomials and Degree
topics.short: The minimal polynomial of α over F is the monic irreducible polynomial with α as a root, and [F(α) : F] equals its degree.

topics.title: Degrees and the Tower Law
topics.short: For fields F ⊆ K ⊆ L, [L : F] = [L : K][K : F]; so [ℚ(√2, √3) : ℚ] = 4, and the cube root of 2 lies in no extension of ℚ whose degree is a power of 2.

topics.title: Finite Fields GF(pⁿ)
topics.short: GF(pⁿ) = ℤₚ[x]/(f) for an irreducible f of degree n: add and multiply polynomials mod p and mod f, and find inverses with the Euclidean algorithm.

topics.title: The Multiplicative Group of a Finite Field
topics.short: The nonzero elements of GF(pⁿ) form a cyclic group of order pⁿ − 1, generated by a primitive element, and GF(pⁿ) contains GF(pᵐ) exactly when m divides n.

topics.short: arg z is a whole family of angles θ + 2πk; the principal value Arg z lies in (−π, π], and Arg(zw) can differ from Arg z + Arg w by 2π.

topics.short: Write f(z) = u(x, y) + i v(x, y): for f(z) = z², u = x² − y² and v = 2xy.

topics.short: Watch f move points from the z-plane to the w-plane: az + b rotates, scales and shifts, z² squares lengths and doubles angles, and 1/z turns the plane inside out.

topics.title: Limits and Continuity
topics.short: lim f(z) = L when f(z) approaches L along every path to z₀; z̄/z has no limit at 0.

topics.title: The Complex Derivative
topics.short: f′(z₀) = lim (f(z₀ + h) − f(z₀))/h as h → 0 from every direction in the plane; z² is differentiable everywhere, and z̄ nowhere.

topics.title: The Cauchy–Riemann Equations
topics.short: f = u + iv with continuous partial derivatives is differentiable exactly where uₓ = v_y and u_y = −vₓ, and there f′ = uₓ + i vₓ.

topics.title: Analytic Functions
topics.short: f is analytic on an open set when it is differentiable at every point of it; sums, products, quotients and compositions follow the usual rules, and polynomials are entire.

topics.title: Harmonic Functions and Harmonic Conjugates
topics.short: The real and imaginary parts of an analytic function solve u_xx + u_yy = 0; given u, find v from the Cauchy–Riemann equations.

topics.title: The Complex Exponential
topics.short: e^z = eˣ(cos y + i sin y): |e^z| = eˣ, e^z is never 0, and it repeats with period 2πi.

topics.title: Complex Sine and Cosine
topics.short: cos z = (e^(iz) + e^(−iz))/2 and sin z = (e^(iz) − e^(−iz))/(2i) are entire and unbounded, so sin z = 2 has solutions.

topics.title: The Complex Logarithm
topics.short: log z = ln|z| + i arg z has infinitely many values, 2πi apart; the principal value is Log z = ln|z| + i Arg z.

topics.title: Branches and Branch Cuts
topics.short: A branch chooses one value continuously on a cut plane: Log jumps by 2πi across its cut, the negative real axis, and a different cut gives a different branch.

topics.title: Complex Powers
topics.short: z^c = e^(c log z) can have many values: every value of i^i = e^(−π/2 − 2πk) is a real number.

topics.title: Contours and Parametrizations
topics.short: Describe segments and circles as z(t): z(t) = a + re^(it), 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π, goes once around the circle counterclockwise.

topics.title: Contour Integrals
topics.short: ∫_C f(z) dz = ∫ f(z(t)) z′(t) dt; once around the unit circle, ∮ dz/z = 2πi.

topics.title: Bounding Integrals: The ML Inequality
topics.short: |∫_C f(z) dz| ≤ M · L, where M bounds |f| on C and L is the length of C.

topics.title: Antiderivatives and Path Independence
topics.short: If F′ = f on an open set containing C, then ∫_C f dz = F(end) − F(start); 1/z has no antiderivative on any loop around 0.

topics.title: Cauchy's Theorem
topics.short: If f is analytic on and inside a simple closed contour C, then ∮_C f(z) dz = 0.

topics.title: Deforming Contours
topics.short: An integral does not change when the contour slides across places where f is analytic, so ∮ dz/(z − a)ⁿ around a is 2πi for n = 1 and 0 for every other integer n.

topics.title: Cauchy's Integral Formula
topics.short: If f is analytic on and inside C and a is inside C, then f(a) = (1/(2πi)) ∮_C f(z)/(z − a) dz.

topics.title: Cauchy's Formula for Derivatives
topics.short: ∮_C f(z)/(z − a)^(n + 1) dz = 2πi f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)/n!, so an analytic function has derivatives of every order.

topics.title: Liouville's Theorem and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
topics.short: A bounded entire function is constant, so every nonconstant polynomial has a complex root.

topics.title: The Maximum Modulus Principle
topics.short: On a bounded region, a nonconstant analytic function that is continuous up to the boundary reaches its largest |f| on the boundary, never inside.

topics.title: Power Series and Disks of Convergence
topics.short: Σ cₙ(z − a)ⁿ converges inside a disk and diverges outside it; find the radius with the ratio or root test.

topics.title: Taylor Series of Analytic Functions
topics.short: An analytic function equals its Taylor series on the largest open disk around a that avoids its singularities.

topics.title: Laurent Series
topics.short: In an annulus, f = Σ cₙ(z − a)ⁿ with negative powers too: 1/(z(z − 1)) has one series on 0 < |z| < 1 and another on |z| > 1.

topics.title: Zeros and Isolated Singularities
topics.short: Classify an isolated singularity as removable, a pole of order m or essential, from the Laurent series or from limits.

topics.title: Residues at Simple Poles
topics.short: The residue at a is the coefficient of 1/(z − a); at a simple pole it is lim (z − a) f(z), which is g(a)/h′(a) when f = g/h.

topics.title: Residues at Higher-Order Poles
topics.short: At a pole of order m, the residue is (1/(m − 1)!) times the limit of the (m − 1)st derivative of (z − a)ᵐ f(z).

topics.title: The Residue Theorem
topics.short: ∮_C f(z) dz = 2πi times the sum of the residues of f at the poles inside C.

topics.title: Integrals over a Full Turn
topics.short: Turn ∫₀^{2π} R(cos θ, sin θ) dθ into a contour integral around the unit circle with z = e^(iθ), cos θ = (z + 1/z)/2 and dθ = dz/(iz).

topics.title: Improper Integrals with Residues
topics.short: Close the real line with a large half-circle in the upper half-plane; when deg Q ≥ deg P + 2, the arc adds nothing as the radius grows, so ∫ P/Q dx is 2πi times the upper residues.

topics.title: Integrals with Sines and Cosines
topics.short: For ∫ R(x) cos(ax) dx with a > 0, integrate R(z) e^(iaz) around the upper half-disk and take the real part.

topics.title: The Argument Principle
topics.short: (1/(2πi)) ∮_C f′/f dz counts the zeros minus the poles inside C, which is the number of times f(C) winds around 0.

topics.title: Rouché's Theorem

topics.title: Congruence and Rigid Motions
topics.short: Two figures are congruent when a rigid motion maps one onto the other.

topics.title: Corresponding Parts
topics.short: In △ABC ≅ △DEF, the letters tell which parts match.

topics.title: SSS, SAS and ASA
topics.short: Three well-chosen parts are enough, and rigid motions show why.

topics.title: AAS and Hypotenuse-Leg
topics.short: Two more shortcuts, including one for right triangles.

topics.title: Proofs with Congruent Triangles
topics.short: Prove triangles congruent, then use matching parts.

topics.title: Triangle Sum and Exterior Angle Proofs
topics.short: Prove the angle sum is 180° and the exterior angle theorem.

topics.title: Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
topics.short: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and the converse holds.

topics.title: Perpendicular Bisectors and the Circumcenter
topics.short: Points on a perpendicular bisector are equally far from the endpoints.

topics.title: Incenter, Centroid and Orthocenter
topics.short: Angle bisectors, medians and altitudes each meet at one point.

topics.title: Triangle Midsegments
topics.short: A midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.

topics.title: Polygon Angle Sums
topics.short: Split a polygon into triangles: (n − 2) × 180°.

topics.title: Properties of Parallelograms
topics.short: Opposite sides and angles are equal, and diagonals bisect each other.

topics.title: Proving a Quadrilateral Is a Parallelogram
topics.short: Use one of the tests, like two pairs of opposite sides equal.

topics.title: Rectangles, Rhombuses and Squares
topics.short: Equal diagonals mean a rectangle; perpendicular diagonals mean a rhombus.

topics.title: Proofs with Coordinates
topics.short: Use slope, distance and midpoint to prove facts about figures.

topics.title: Properties of Dilations
topics.short: A dilation keeps lines parallel and multiplies lengths by k.

topics.title: Similarity Through Transformations
topics.short: Two figures are similar if a dilation and rigid motions map one to the other.

topics.title: Proving AA Similarity
topics.short: Two pairs of equal angles make triangles similar.

topics.title: SSS and SAS Similarity
topics.short: Proportional sides, with or without an included angle, prove similarity.

topics.title: The Triangle Proportionality Theorem
topics.short: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally.

topics.title: Dividing a Segment in a Ratio
topics.short: Find the point that splits a segment in the ratio a : b.

topics.title: Similar Right Triangles and the Geometric Mean
topics.short: The altitude to the hypotenuse makes three similar triangles.

topics.title: Proving the Pythagorean Theorem with Similarity
topics.short: Use the three similar triangles to prove a² + b² = c².

topics.title: 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 Triangles
topics.short: Their sides are in fixed ratios: 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2.

topics.title: Sine, Cosine and Tangent
topics.short: Similar triangles make side ratios depend only on the angle.

topics.title: Sine and Cosine of Complementary Angles
topics.short: sin A = cos(90° − A).

topics.title: Solving Right Triangles
topics.short: Find missing sides with trig ratios and the Pythagorean theorem.

topics.title: Finding Angles with Inverse Trig
topics.short: Use sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ to find an angle from a ratio.

topics.title: Angles of Elevation and Depression
topics.short: Model heights and distances with right triangles.

topics.title: Triangle Area with Sine
topics.short: Area = ½ab sin C.

topics.title: The Law of Sines
topics.short: Sides are proportional to the sines of their opposite angles.

topics.title: The Law of Cosines
topics.short: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C extends the Pythagorean theorem.

topics.title: Parts of a Circle
topics.short: Radius, diameter, chord, arc, tangent and secant.

topics.title: Central Angles and Arcs
topics.short: An arc's measure equals its central angle; all circles are similar.

topics.title: Inscribed Angles
topics.short: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.

topics.title: Tangent Lines
topics.short: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

topics.title: Inscribed Quadrilaterals
topics.short: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to 180°.

topics.title: Arc Length
topics.short: An arc is a fraction of the circumference: (θ/360) · 2πr.

topics.title: Sector Area
topics.short: A sector is a fraction of the circle's area.

topics.title: Equation of a Circle
topics.short: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² comes from the distance formula.

topics.title: Finding the Center by Completing the Square
topics.short: Rewrite x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 in center-radius form.

topics.title: Parabola from Focus and Directrix
topics.short: A parabola is all points equally far from a point and a line.

topics.title: Area of Regular Polygons
topics.short: Area = ½ × apothem × perimeter.

topics.title: Perimeter and Area on the Coordinate Plane
topics.short: Use the distance formula to find perimeters and areas.

topics.title: Cavalieri's Principle
topics.short: Solids with equal cross-sections at every height have equal volume.

topics.title: Volume of Pyramids, Cones and Spheres
topics.short: Use V = ⅓Bh for pyramids and cones and V = (4/3)πr³ for spheres.

topics.title: Surface Area of Solids
topics.short: Find surface areas of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.

topics.title: Cross Sections and Solids of Revolution
topics.short: Identify slices of solids and the solid made by spinning a shape.

topics.title: Scaling Area and Volume
topics.short: Scale lengths by k: areas scale by k², volumes by k³.

topics.title: Modeling, Density and Design
topics.short: Model objects with shapes, use density, and solve design problems.

topics.title: Counting to 10
topics.short: Say the numbers from 1 to 10 in order.

topics.title: Touch and Count
topics.short: Say exactly one number for each object you touch.

topics.title: The Last Number Tells How Many
topics.short: The last number you say is how many there are.

topics.title: Seeing Small Amounts at a Glance
topics.short: Know 1 to 5 dots without counting them one by one.

topics.title: Reading and Writing 0 to 10
topics.short: Match a written number to a group of objects; 0 means none.

topics.title: One More
topics.short: Each counting number is one more than the number before it.

topics.title: Counting Objects to 20
topics.short: Count up to 20 things in a line, a rectangle or a circle.

topics.title: Counting Out a Number
topics.short: Give exactly the number of objects asked for.

topics.title: Numbers 11 to 20
topics.short: Read and write the teen numbers and 20.

topics.title: Counting On from Any Number
topics.short: Start counting from a number other than 1.

topics.title: Counting to 100 by Ones and Tens
topics.short: Count by ones and by tens all the way to 100.

topics.title: More, Fewer or the Same
topics.short: Match or count to compare two groups.

topics.title: Comparing Numbers to 10
topics.short: Tell which of two written numbers is greater.

topics.title: Putting Together
topics.short: Adding means joining groups to find how many in all.

topics.title: Taking Away
topics.short: Subtracting means taking some away and counting what is left.

topics.title: Writing +, − and =
topics.short: Write a number sentence that matches a story or picture.

topics.title: Story Problems within 10
topics.short: Act out, draw and solve adding and subtracting stories.

topics.title: Breaking Apart Numbers
topics.short: Split a number like 5 into 2 and 3, or 4 and 1.

topics.title: Making 10
topics.short: Find the number that goes with another to make 10.

topics.title: Quick Facts within 5
topics.short: Add and subtract within 5 quickly.

topics.title: Teen Numbers Are Ten and Some More
topics.short: 14 is ten ones and four more ones.

topics.title: Long, Tall and Heavy
topics.short: Describe things by length, height or weight.

topics.title: Comparing Lengths and Weights
topics.short: Line things up, or hold them, to see which is longer or heavier.

topics.title: Sorting and Counting
topics.short: Sort objects into groups, count each group and order them.

topics.title: Position Words
topics.short: Use words like above, below, beside, in front of and behind.

topics.title: Naming Flat Shapes
topics.short: Name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles and hexagons.

topics.title: Flat and Solid Shapes
topics.short: Tell flat shapes from solid shapes like cubes, cones, cylinders and spheres.

topics.title: Sides and Corners
topics.short: Compare shapes by counting their sides and corners.

topics.title: Building and Combining Shapes
topics.short: Make shapes from parts, and put small shapes together to make bigger ones.

topics.title: Linear Systems and Their Pictures
topics.short: See a system as intersecting lines and planes, or as combining columns.

topics.title: Augmented Matrices and Row Operations
topics.short: Swap, scale and add rows without changing the solutions.

topics.title: Gaussian Elimination and Echelon Form
topics.short: Clear entries below each pivot.

topics.title: Reduced Row Echelon Form
topics.short: Make every pivot 1 with zeros above and below.

topics.title: Free Variables and Parametric Solutions
topics.short: Write every solution in terms of the free variables.

topics.title: When Solutions Exist and Are Unique
topics.short: Read the answer from the pivot positions.

topics.title: Vectors in Rⁿ and Linear Combinations
topics.short: Scale and add vectors to reach new ones.

topics.title: Span
topics.short: The span is every linear combination of a set of vectors.

topics.title: The Matrix Equation Ax = b
topics.short: Ax is a combination of the columns of A.

topics.title: Homogeneous Systems
topics.short: Ax = 0 always has the zero solution; the question is whether there are others.

topics.title: Linear Independence
topics.short: No vector in the set is a combination of the others.

topics.title: Matrix Operations and Transposes
topics.short: Add, multiply and transpose, minding the order.

topics.title: Inverses by Gauss–Jordan
topics.short: Row-reduce A next to I until A becomes I; then I has become A⁻¹.

topics.title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem
topics.short: Many statements about a square matrix are all true or all false together.

topics.title: Elementary Matrices and LU Factorization
topics.short: Record elimination as A = LU.

topics.title: Linear Transformations
topics.short: T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v) and T(cu) = cT(u).

topics.title: The Matrix of a Linear Transformation
topics.short: The columns are the images of the standard basis vectors.

topics.title: Rotations, Reflections, Shears and Projections
topics.short: Read and build matrices for common plane maps.

topics.title: Composition as Matrix Multiplication
topics.short: Doing S after T has matrix ST.

topics.title: One-to-One and Onto
topics.short: Pivots in every column mean one-to-one; in every row mean onto.

topics.title: Neural Network Layers: Matrices and Switches
topics.short: A layer computes ReLU(Wx + b); stack two and you can trace the whole network by hand.

topics.title: Determinants by Cofactor Expansion
topics.short: Expand along any row or column.

topics.title: Properties of Determinants
topics.short: Row operations change the determinant in predictable ways; det(AB) = det A det B.

topics.title: Determinants as Area and Volume
topics.short: |det A| is the factor by which A scales area or volume.

topics.title: Cramer's Rule and the Adjugate
topics.short: Solve small systems and invert with determinants.

topics.title: Writing Short Proofs
topics.short: Prove statements from definitions, one justified step at a time.

topics.title: Vector Spaces and Subspaces
topics.short: A subspace contains 0 and is closed under addition and scaling.

topics.title: Null Space and Column Space
topics.short: Nul A solves Ax = 0; Col A is the span of the columns.

topics.title: Bases
topics.short: A basis spans and is independent.

topics.title: Dimension and Rank
topics.short: Every basis has the same size; rank is the dimension of the column space.

topics.title: The Rank–Nullity Theorem and the Four Subspaces
topics.short: rank + nullity = number of columns.

topics.title: Coordinates and Change of Basis
topics.short: Describe vectors in a new basis with a change-of-coordinates matrix.

topics.title: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
topics.short: Av = λv: A only stretches v.

topics.title: The Characteristic Equation
topics.short: Solve det(A − λI) = 0.

topics.title: Eigenspaces and Multiplicity
topics.short: Each eigenvalue has a space of eigenvectors.

topics.title: Diagonalization
topics.short: A = PDP⁻¹ when there are enough independent eigenvectors.

topics.title: Matrix Powers and Markov Chains
topics.short: Use Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹ and find steady states.

topics.title: Complex Eigenvalues
topics.short: Complex eigenvalues signal rotation.

topics.title: Similar Matrices
topics.short: Similar matrices describe the same map in different bases.

topics.title: Length and Orthogonality in Rⁿ
topics.short: Vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is 0.

topics.title: Orthogonal Complements
topics.short: Row space and null space are perpendicular.

topics.title: Orthogonal Projections
topics.short: Find the closest point in a subspace.

topics.title: Gram–Schmidt and QR
topics.short: Turn any basis into an orthonormal one.

topics.title: Least Squares
topics.short: Solve AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb to fit data.

topics.title: Orthogonal Matrices
topics.short: QᵀQ = I: rotations and reflections preserve length.

topics.title: Symmetric Matrices and the Spectral Theorem
topics.short: A symmetric matrix has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors.

topics.title: Quadratic Forms and Positive Definite Matrices
topics.short: xᵀAx > 0 for all x ≠ 0 exactly when all eigenvalues are positive.

topics.title: The Singular Value Decomposition
topics.short: A = UΣVᵀ for every matrix.

topics.title: Low-Rank Approximation and Applications
topics.short: Keep the largest singular values to compress data.

topics.title: Divisibility
topics.short: a ∣ b means b = ak for some integer k; if a divides b and c, it divides every combination mb + nc.

topics.title: The Division Algorithm
topics.short: For a positive divisor b, every integer a can be written as a = bq + r with 0 ≤ r < b, even when a is negative.

topics.title: Writing Numbers in Other Bases
topics.short: Convert to base b by dividing by b again and again, then read the remainders from last to first.

topics.title: The Euclidean Algorithm
topics.short: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r), where r is the remainder when a is divided by b; repeat until the remainder is 0.

topics.title: Bézout's Identity and the Extended Euclidean Algorithm
topics.short: Work the Euclidean algorithm backward to write gcd(a, b) = ax + by.

topics.title: Linear Diophantine Equations
topics.short: ax + by = c has integer solutions exactly when d = gcd(a, b) divides c, and then x = x₀ + (b/d)t, y = y₀ − (a/d)t.

topics.title: Testing Primes and the Sieve of Eratosthenes
topics.short: n is prime when no prime up to √n divides it; the sieve crosses out multiples to list every prime up to N.

topics.title: Unique Prime Factorization
topics.short: Every integer above 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, because a prime that divides ab divides a or b (Euclid's lemma).

topics.title: gcd and lcm from Prime Factorizations
topics.short: Take the smaller exponent of each prime for the gcd and the larger for the lcm; then gcd(a, b) · lcm(a, b) = ab.

topics.title: Counting and Adding Divisors
topics.short: If n = p₁^a₁ ⋯ pₖ^aₖ, then n has (a₁ + 1)⋯(aₖ + 1) divisors, and their sum σ(n) is a product of geometric sums.

topics.title: Perfect Numbers and Mersenne Primes
topics.short: n is perfect when σ(n) = 2n; whenever 2ᵖ − 1 is prime, 2ᵖ⁻¹(2ᵖ − 1) is perfect.

topics.title: Prime Powers in n!
topics.short: The exponent of p in n! is ⌊n/p⌋ + ⌊n/p²⌋ + ⌊n/p³⌋ + ⋯, so 100! ends in 24 zeros.

topics.title: Infinitely Many Primes
topics.short: Euclid's argument: p₁p₂⋯pₖ + 1 has a prime factor that is not on the list p₁, …, pₖ.

topics.title: How Common Are Primes?
topics.short: The prime number theorem: there are about x/ln x primes up to x. Primes thin out, and n! + 2, …, n! + n is a run of n − 1 composite numbers.

topics.title: Congruence mod n
topics.short: a ≡ b (mod n) when n ∣ (a − b), that is, when a and b leave the same remainder on division by n.

topics.title: Arithmetic mod n
topics.short: Reduce first, then add, subtract and multiply: the result is the same as reducing at the end.

topics.title: Divisibility Tests from Congruences
topics.short: Since 10 ≡ 1 (mod 9) and 10 ≡ −1 (mod 11), digit sums and alternating digit sums test divisibility by 9 and by 11.

topics.title: Fast Powers mod n
topics.short: Square again and again, multiply the powers that match the binary digits of the exponent, and reduce after every step.

topics.title: Modular Inverses
topics.short: a has an inverse mod n exactly when gcd(a, n) = 1; find it with the extended Euclidean algorithm.

topics.title: Linear Congruences
topics.short: ax ≡ b (mod n) has no solution unless d = gcd(a, n) divides b, and then it has exactly d solutions mod n.

topics.title: The Chinese Remainder Theorem
topics.short: When m and n are coprime, the pair x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) has exactly one solution mod mn.

topics.title: Fermat's Little Theorem
topics.short: If p is prime and p ∤ a, then aᵖ⁻¹ ≡ 1 (mod p), so exponents can be reduced mod p − 1.

topics.title: Wilson's Theorem
topics.short: An integer p > 1 is prime exactly when (p − 1)! ≡ −1 (mod p): the factors from 2 to p − 2 pair up with their inverses, leaving 1 · (p − 1) ≡ −1.

topics.title: Euler's Phi Function
topics.short: φ(n) counts the k from 1 to n with gcd(k, n) = 1; φ(pᵏ) = pᵏ − pᵏ⁻¹, and φ(mn) = φ(m)φ(n) when gcd(m, n) = 1.

topics.title: Euler's Theorem
topics.short: If gcd(a, n) = 1, then a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n); use it to find the last digits of huge powers.

topics.title: Fermat Tests and Pseudoprimes
topics.short: If aⁿ⁻¹ ≢ 1 (mod n) for some a with 1 < a < n, then n is composite; passing the test does not prove that n is prime.

topics.title: The Order of an Element
topics.short: The order of a mod n is the smallest k > 0 with aᵏ ≡ 1; it divides φ(n), and the powers of a repeat with that period.

topics.title: Primitive Roots
topics.short: g is a primitive root mod p when its order is p − 1, so its powers reach every nonzero residue; check that g^((p − 1)/q) ≢ 1 for each prime q dividing p − 1.

topics.title: Discrete Logarithms
topics.short: With a primitive root g mod p, every nonzero residue is gᵏ for exactly one k mod p − 1; checking a k is easy, finding one is slow.

topics.title: Shift and Affine Ciphers
topics.short: Encrypt letters with x ↦ ax + b (mod 26) and decrypt with x ↦ a⁻¹(x − b); a must be coprime to 26.

topics.title: Diffie–Hellman Key Exchange
topics.short: Two people agree on a secret g^(ab) mod p while sharing only gᵃ and gᵇ in public.

topics.title: The RSA Cryptosystem
topics.short: The public key is (n, e) with n = pq; the private key d ≡ e⁻¹ (mod φ(n)); encrypt with c ≡ mᵉ and decrypt with m ≡ cᵈ (mod n).

topics.title: Squares mod p
topics.short: a is a quadratic residue mod p when x² ≡ a has a solution; for an odd prime p, exactly half of the nonzero residues are squares.

topics.title: The Legendre Symbol and Euler's Criterion
topics.short: For p ∤ a, (a/p) is 1 when a is a square mod p and −1 when it is not, and (a/p) ≡ a^((p − 1)/2) (mod p).

topics.title: Is −1 or 2 a Square mod p?
topics.short: −1 is a square mod an odd prime p exactly when p ≡ 1 (mod 4), and 2 is a square exactly when p ≡ ±1 (mod 8).

topics.title: Quadratic Reciprocity
topics.short: For odd primes p ≠ q, (p/q) = (q/p), except when p ≡ q ≡ 3 (mod 4), when (p/q) = −(q/p).

topics.title: Pythagorean Triples
topics.short: Every primitive triple is (m² − n², 2mn, m² + n²), up to the order of the legs, with m > n > 0, m and n coprime and of opposite parity.

topics.title: Sums of Two Squares
topics.short: n is a sum of two squares exactly when every prime ≡ 3 (mod 4) appears in its factorization to an even power.

topics.title: Continued Fractions of Rational Numbers
topics.short: The quotients of the Euclidean algorithm give a/b = [q₀; q₁, q₂, …], and the convergents are better and better approximations.

topics.title: Continued Fractions of Square Roots
topics.short: When d is not a perfect square, √d has a repeating continued fraction, and its convergents are the best rational approximations: no fraction with a smaller denominator comes closer.

topics.title: Pell's Equation
topics.short: For d > 0 not a perfect square, x² − dy² = 1 has a smallest solution with y > 0, found among the convergents of √d, and the powers of x₁ + y₁√d give all the others.

topics.title: Absolute and Relative Error
topics.short: Absolute error is |approximation − true value|; relative error divides by |true value| and tells how many significant digits are correct.

topics.title: Binary Fractions
topics.short: Convert a decimal fraction to base 2 by doubling and keeping the whole-number parts: 0.1 becomes 0.000110011… and never ends.

topics.title: Floating-Point Numbers
topics.short: A float stores ±1.f × 2ᵉ with a fixed number of bits, so the gaps between floats grow with their size; machine epsilon, 2⁻⁵² ≈ 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶ in double precision, sets the relative precision.

topics.title: Round-Off and Cancellation
topics.short: Subtracting nearly equal numbers wipes out correct digits; rewrite the formula to avoid it, as in √(x + 1) − √x = 1/(√(x + 1) + √x).

topics.title: Truncation Error and Order of Accuracy
topics.short: Stopping an infinite process, such as a Taylor series or a limit, leaves truncation error; an error of order hᵖ shrinks by a factor of about 2ᵖ when h is halved.

topics.title: Conditioning of a Problem
topics.short: The condition number κ = |x f′(x)/f(x)| says how much a relative change in the input is magnified in the output, whatever method is used.

topics.title: Stable and Unstable Algorithms
topics.short: A stable algorithm gives the exact answer to a slightly changed problem, so two formulas for the same quantity can behave very differently in floating point.

topics.title: Horner's Method
topics.short: Evaluate a polynomial by nesting, ((aₙx + aₙ₋₁)x + ⋯)x + a₀, with only n multiplications and n additions.

topics.title: The Bisection Method
topics.short: Keep halving an interval where f changes sign; after n steps the midpoint is within (b − a)/2ⁿ⁺¹ of a root.

topics.title: Fixed-Point Iteration
topics.short: Rewrite f(x) = 0 as x = g(x) and repeat xₙ₊₁ = g(xₙ); it converges near the fixed point when |g′| < 1 there.

topics.title: Order of Convergence
topics.short: If eₙ₊₁ ≈ C eₙᵖ, the method has order p: a linear method gains about the same number of digits each step, and a quadratic one doubles them.

topics.title: Newton's Method: Speed and Failure
topics.short: Near a simple root, Newton's method converges quadratically; a poor start, a tangent that is nearly flat, or a multiple root can make it fail or slow down.

topics.title: The Secant Method
topics.short: Replace f′ with the slope through the last two points; it needs no derivative, and its order is about 1.618.

topics.title: Newton's Method for Systems
topics.short: Solve J(x) Δ = −F(x) with the Jacobian matrix J, then update x to x + Δ.

topics.title: The Cost of Elimination
topics.short: Gaussian elimination takes about 2n³/3 arithmetic operations and each triangular solve about n², so doubling n multiplies the work by about 8.

topics.title: Partial Pivoting
topics.short: Before each elimination step, swap up the row whose entry in the pivot column is largest in size, so tiny pivots do not magnify round-off.

topics.title: Solving with PA = LU
topics.short: Factor once with pivoting, then solve Ly = Pb by forward substitution and Ux = y by back substitution for each new right-hand side b.

topics.title: Vector and Matrix Norms
topics.short: Measure size with ‖x‖₁, ‖x‖₂ and ‖x‖∞; the matching matrix norms ‖A‖₁ and ‖A‖∞ are the largest absolute column sum and the largest absolute row sum.

topics.title: The Condition Number of a Matrix
topics.short: κ(A) = ‖A‖ ‖A⁻¹‖ bounds how much a relative change in b can grow in x; a small residual does not guarantee a small error.

topics.title: Jacobi Iteration
topics.short: Solve each equation for its own variable and update every variable at once from the previous values; strict diagonal dominance guarantees convergence.

topics.title: Gauss–Seidel Iteration
topics.short: Use each new value as soon as it is computed; for strictly diagonally dominant systems it converges, usually faster than Jacobi.

topics.title: Lagrange Interpolation
topics.short: Exactly one polynomial of degree at most n passes through n + 1 points with different x-values; build it from basis polynomials that are 1 at one node and 0 at the others.

topics.title: Newton's Divided Differences
topics.short: Build the interpolating polynomial one point at a time from a table of divided differences, without starting over.

topics.title: Interpolation Error
topics.short: f(x) − p(x) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)/(n + 1)! · (x − x₀)(x − x₁)⋯(x − xₙ) for some ξ in the interval.

topics.title: Runge's Phenomenon and Chebyshev Nodes
topics.short: High-degree interpolation at equally spaced points can swing wildly near the ends; Chebyshev nodes, bunched toward the ends, fix it.

topics.title: Cubic Splines
topics.short: Join cubic pieces that match values, slopes and second derivatives at the knots; a natural spline has second derivative 0 at both ends.

topics.title: Finite-Difference Derivatives
topics.short: The forward difference (f(x + h) − f(x))/h has error of order h; the central difference (f(x + h) − f(x − h))/(2h) has error of order h².

topics.title: The Best Step Size
topics.short: Shrinking h cuts truncation error but magnifies round-off, so the total error is smallest at a moderate h, about 10⁻⁸ for a forward difference in double precision.

topics.title: Richardson Extrapolation
topics.short: Combine results at h and h/2 to cancel the leading error term: for a method with error of order h², use (4A(h/2) − A(h))/3.

topics.title: Error in the Trapezoid and Simpson's Rules
topics.short: The composite trapezoid rule has error of order h² and Simpson's rule of order h⁴, so halving h cuts the error by about 4 or 16.

topics.title: Romberg Integration
topics.short: Apply Richardson extrapolation to trapezoid estimates again and again to fill a triangle of better and better values.

topics.title: Gaussian Quadrature
topics.short: Choose the nodes as well as the weights: two points at ±1/√3 integrate every cubic exactly on [−1, 1].

topics.title: Adaptive Integration
topics.short: Compare Simpson's rule on an interval with Simpson's rule on its two halves; the difference divided by 15 estimates the error, and only the intervals that fail the test are split.

topics.title: Local and Global Error
topics.short: Each Euler step makes a local error of order h², and the 1/h steps together leave a global error of order h.

topics.title: Systems and Higher-Order Equations
topics.short: Rewrite y″ = f(t, y, y′) as a first-order system, then take Euler or Runge–Kutta steps with vectors.

topics.title: Stability of Euler's Method
topics.short: For y′ = λy with λ < 0, Euler's method gives yₙ = (1 + hλ)ⁿ y₀, which stays bounded only when |1 + hλ| ≤ 1, that is, when h ≤ 2/|λ|.

topics.title: Backward Euler and Stiff Equations
topics.short: Backward Euler uses the slope at the new point, so each step means solving for yₙ₊₁; for y′ = λy with λ < 0 it is stable for every step size.

topics.title: Multistep Methods
topics.short: Adams–Bashforth methods reuse earlier slopes, as in yₙ₊₁ = yₙ + (h/2)(3fₙ − fₙ₋₁), and need a one-step method to get started.

topics.title: Boundary Value Problems by Finite Differences
topics.short: Replace y″ by (yᵢ₊₁ − 2yᵢ + yᵢ₋₁)/h² at each inside grid point to get a tridiagonal linear system.

topics.title: The Heat Equation: An Explicit Scheme
topics.short: uᵢⁿ⁺¹ = uᵢⁿ + r(uᵢ₊₁ⁿ − 2uᵢⁿ + uᵢ₋₁ⁿ) with r = kΔt/Δx² is stable only when r ≤ 1/2.

topics.title: Least Squares with QR
topics.short: Solve Rx = Qᵀb instead of the normal equations, because forming AᵀA squares the condition number.

topics.title: The Power Method
topics.short: Multiply by A and rescale, again and again; the vector turns toward the dominant eigenvector at a rate set by |λ₂/λ₁|.

topics.title: Inverse and Shifted Power Methods
topics.short: Run the power method on (A − sI)⁻¹, solving a system each step instead of inverting, to find the eigenvalue of A closest to the shift s.

topics.title: Gershgorin Disks
topics.short: Every eigenvalue lies in a disk centered at a diagonal entry aᵢᵢ, with radius equal to the sum of the other |aᵢⱼ| in that row.

topics.title: The QR Algorithm
topics.short: Factor Aₖ = QₖRₖ and set Aₖ₊₁ = RₖQₖ; each new matrix is similar to A, and its diagonal approaches the eigenvalues.

topics.title: Counting to 5

topics.title: Touch and Count
topics.short: Say one number for each thing you touch.

topics.title: How Many?
topics.short: The last number you say tells how many.

topics.title: Counting to 10

topics.title: Counting Things to 10
topics.short: Count up to 10 things in rows, circles or a jumble.

topics.title: Find a Group of Some

topics.title: Counting to 20
topics.short: Say the numbers to 20 and count on from 10.

topics.title: At a Glance: 1, 2, 3

topics.title: Finger Numbers

topics.title: Numbers 6 to 10

topics.short: Put the numbers 0 to 10 in order and find a missing one.

topics.short: Tell which group has more.

topics.title: Which Has Fewer?
topics.short: Tell which group has fewer.

topics.title: The Same Number

topics.title: One More
topics.short: One more is the next counting number.

topics.title: Big and Small
topics.short: Find the biggest and the smallest.

topics.title: Tall and Short
topics.short: Compare heights from the same floor.

topics.title: Long and Short
topics.short: Compare lengths from the same start line.

topics.title: Heavy and Light
topics.short: Tell which is heavier or lighter, and read a balance.

topics.title: Measuring with Blocks
topics.short: Measure a length with blocks and compare.

topics.title: Sorting by Color
topics.short: Sort and count things by color.

topics.title: Sorting by Shape
topics.short: Sort and count things by shape.

topics.title: Sorting by Size
topics.short: Sort things into big and small.

topics.title: Which One Does Not Belong?
topics.short: Find the one that is not like the others.

topics.title: AAB and ABB Patterns
topics.short: Find what comes next when one part repeats twice.

topics.title: ABC Patterns

topics.title: Circles and Squares
topics.short: Know a circle and a square, even when turned.

topics.title: Triangles and Rectangles
topics.short: Know a triangle and a rectangle, even when turned.

topics.title: Sides and Corners
topics.short: Count the sides and corners of a shape.

topics.short: Find circles, triangles and rectangles in real things.

topics.short: Say where something is: above, on or under.

topics.title: In Front and Behind
topics.short: Say where something is: in front of or behind.

topics.title: Beside and Between
topics.short: Say where something is: beside or between.

topics.title: First, Next and Last
topics.short: Who is first, next and last in line.

topics.title: What Comes Next?
topics.short: Put the steps of a little story in order.

topics.title: Putting Together
topics.short: Put two small groups together and count them all.

topics.title: Taking Away
topics.short: Take some away and count what is left.

topics.title: Morning, Afternoon and Night
topics.short: Tell the times of day from the sky.

topics.title: Our Day in Order
topics.short: Put the things we do in a day in order.

topics.title: Looking at Coins
topics.short: Look at coins and count pennies.

topics.title: Angles in Standard Position
topics.short: Draw angles from the positive x-axis, including negative and coterminal angles.

topics.title: Radian Measure
topics.short: One radian is the angle whose arc equals the radius.

topics.title: Converting Degrees and Radians
topics.short: Multiply by π/180 or 180/π.

topics.title: Arc Length, Sector Area and Angular Speed
topics.short: s = rθ and A = ½r²θ when θ is in radians.

topics.title: Sine and Cosine on the Unit Circle
topics.short: (cos θ, sin θ) is the point at angle θ on the unit circle.

topics.title: Exact Values at Special Angles
topics.short: Use 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles to find exact values.

topics.title: Reference Angles and Signs by Quadrant
topics.short: Find values in any quadrant from a reference angle and a sign.

topics.title: Symmetry and Periodicity
topics.short: sin(−θ) = −sin θ, cos(−θ) = cos θ, and both repeat every 2π.

topics.title: All Six Trig Functions
topics.short: Tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant from sine and cosine.

topics.title: The Pythagorean Identity
topics.short: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and finding one value from another.

topics.title: Graphs of Sine and Cosine
topics.short: Unroll the unit circle into a wave.

topics.title: Amplitude and Period
topics.short: In y = A sin(Bx), the amplitude is |A| and the period is 2π/B.

topics.title: Phase Shift and Midline
topics.short: y = A sin(B(x − h)) + k shifts by h and centers on y = k.

topics.title: Modeling with Sinusoids
topics.short: Fit a sine curve to tides, daylight and Ferris wheels.

topics.title: Graphs of Tangent, Secant and Cosecant
topics.short: Find asymptotes where cosine or sine is zero.

topics.title: Damped Oscillation
topics.short: Multiply a sinusoid by a decaying exponential.

topics.title: Inverse Trig Functions
topics.short: Restrict sine, cosine and tangent so they have inverses.

topics.title: Compositions with Inverse Trig
topics.short: Evaluate expressions like sin⁻¹(sin 5π/6) and cos(tan⁻¹ x).

topics.title: Reciprocal, Quotient and Pythagorean Identities
topics.short: Rewrite trig expressions in terms of sine and cosine.

topics.title: Verifying Identities
topics.short: Transform one side until it matches the other.

topics.title: Sum and Difference Formulas
topics.short: sin(a + b) = sin a cos b + cos a sin b.

topics.title: Double-Angle Formulas
topics.short: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and three forms of cos 2θ.

topics.title: Half-Angle and Power-Reducing Formulas
topics.short: Rewrite sin²θ and cos²θ in terms of cos 2θ.

topics.title: Solving Basic Trig Equations
topics.short: Find every solution in one period, then all solutions.

topics.title: Trig Equations with Factoring and Multiple Angles
topics.short: Factor, use identities, and handle 2θ and 3θ.

topics.title: The Ambiguous Case
topics.short: With two sides and a non-included angle there may be 0, 1 or 2 triangles.

topics.title: Bearings and Triangle Applications
topics.short: Solve navigation and surveying problems with the laws of sines and cosines.

topics.title: Heron's Formula
topics.short: Find a triangle's area from its three sides.

topics.title: Vectors
topics.short: A vector has a size and a direction.

topics.title: Vector Components and Magnitude
topics.short: v = ⟨|v| cos θ, |v| sin θ⟩.

topics.title: Adding and Scaling Vectors
topics.short: Add tip to tail; scaling stretches or flips.

topics.title: Velocity and Force Problems
topics.short: Find a resultant for wind, current and forces.

topics.title: The Dot Product and the Angle Between Vectors
topics.short: u · v = |u||v| cos θ.

topics.title: Vector Projections and Work
topics.short: Split a vector into parts along and across another vector.

topics.title: Polar Coordinates
topics.short: Locate points by distance r and angle θ.

topics.title: Converting Polar and Rectangular
topics.short: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, and back again.

topics.title: Graphs of Polar Equations
topics.short: Sketch circles, cardioids, roses and limaçons.

topics.title: Complex Numbers in the Plane
topics.short: Plot a + bi and find its modulus.

topics.title: Polar Form of a Complex Number
topics.short: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ).

topics.title: Multiplying, Powers and De Moivre's Theorem
topics.short: Multiply moduli and add angles; zⁿ = rⁿ(cos nθ + i sin nθ).

topics.title: nth Roots of Complex Numbers
topics.short: A nonzero number has n nth roots spread evenly around a circle.

topics.title: Parametric Equations
topics.short: x and y both depend on a third variable t.

topics.title: Eliminating the Parameter
topics.short: Solve for t or use an identity to get one equation in x and y.

topics.title: Projectile Motion with Parametric Equations
topics.short: Model a launched object with x = v₀t cos θ and y = h + v₀t sin θ − 16t².

topics.title: Parabolas as Conics
topics.short: Use focus, directrix and vertex for parabolas opening any way.

topics.title: Ellipses
topics.short: The sum of distances to two foci is constant; c² = a² − b².

topics.title: Hyperbolas
topics.short: The difference of distances to two foci is constant; c² = a² + b².

topics.title: Identifying Conics from Equations
topics.short: Complete the square to name and graph any conic.

topics.title: Matrices and Matrix Arithmetic
topics.short: Add matrices and multiply them by numbers.

topics.title: Multiplying Matrices
topics.short: Each entry is a row times a column.

topics.title: Solving Systems with Row Operations
topics.short: Write an augmented matrix and row-reduce it.

topics.title: Determinants of 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 Matrices
topics.short: ad − bc, and expansion by minors.

topics.title: Inverse Matrices
topics.short: A⁻¹ exists exactly when det A ≠ 0.

topics.title: Solving Systems with Inverse Matrices
topics.short: Write AX = B and multiply by A⁻¹ on the left.

topics.title: Matrices as Transformations
topics.short: A 2 × 2 matrix moves the plane, and |det| scales area.

topics.title: Partial Fraction Decomposition
topics.short: Split a rational expression into simpler fractions.

topics.title: Proof by Induction
topics.short: Prove a base case, then show each case implies the next.

topics.title: Logistic Growth
topics.short: Growth that slows near a carrying capacity.

topics.title: The Difference Quotient
topics.short: [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h is the slope of a secant line.

topics.title: The Idea of a Limit
topics.short: A limit is the value a function approaches, not necessarily its value.

topics.title: Estimating Limits from Graphs and Tables
topics.short: Read limits from the left and the right.

topics.title: The Axioms of Probability
topics.short: Every probability rule follows from three: P(A) ≥ 0, P(S) = 1, and the probabilities of disjoint events add.

topics.title: Inclusion–Exclusion for Events
topics.short: P(A ∪ B ∪ C) adds the three probabilities, subtracts the three pairwise overlaps and adds back the triple overlap.

topics.title: Products of Chances: The Birthday Problem
topics.short: Find "at least one match" through its complement, a product of shrinking fractions: in a group of 23, a shared birthday is slightly more likely than not.

topics.title: Conditional or Joint?
topics.short: P(A ∩ B) is the chance that both happen; P(A ∣ B) is the chance of A among the outcomes where B happens. Read the question to see which one it asks for.

topics.title: The Law of Total Probability
topics.short: Split into cases A₁, …, Aₙ that cover every outcome without overlapping: P(B) = Σ P(B ∣ Aᵢ) P(Aᵢ).

topics.title: Bayes' Theorem with Several Causes
topics.short: P(Aⱼ ∣ B) = P(B ∣ Aⱼ) P(Aⱼ) / Σ P(B ∣ Aᵢ) P(Aᵢ), and each new piece of evidence updates the answer again.

topics.title: Independence of Several Events
topics.short: A, B and C are independent when every pair and the triple multiply; disjoint events with positive probabilities are never independent.

topics.title: PMFs and CDFs
topics.short: A pmf lists P(X = x); the CDF F(x) = P(X ≤ x) climbs in steps, and P(a < X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a).

topics.title: Expected Value of a Function
topics.short: E[g(X)] = Σ g(x) P(X = x), and in general E[g(X)] ≠ g(E[X]).

topics.title: Variance: The Shortcut and the Rules
topics.short: Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])², and Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X).

topics.title: Linearity of Expectation and Indicators
topics.short: E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] always, so a count has mean equal to the sum of its indicators' probabilities: a shuffled deck has on average 1 card left in its starting place.

topics.title: Sampling without Replacement: The Hypergeometric Distribution
topics.short: Drawing n from N items, K of them successes: P(X = k) = C(K, k) C(N − K, n − k) / C(N, n).

topics.title: Waiting for the rth Success
topics.short: The number of trials needed for r successes has P(X = k) = C(k − 1, r − 1) pʳ (1 − p)^(k − r) and mean r/p.

topics.title: The Poisson Distribution
topics.short: Counts of rare events in a fixed time or space: P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λᵏ / k!, with mean and variance both λ.

topics.title: The Poisson Approximation to the Binomial
topics.short: When n is large and p is small, Binomial(n, p) is close to Poisson with λ = np.

topics.title: Choosing a Distribution
topics.short: Match the story to binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric or Poisson.

topics.title: Probability Density Functions
topics.short: A density f ≥ 0 has total area 1, and P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx.

topics.title: CDFs, Medians and Percentiles
topics.short: F(x) = ∫ f(t) dt from −∞ to x, f = F′, and the median m solves F(m) = 1/2.

topics.title: Mean and Variance of a Continuous Variable
topics.short: E[X] = ∫ x f(x) dx and E[g(X)] = ∫ g(x) f(x) dx, and the variance shortcut still holds.

topics.title: The Exponential Distribution
topics.short: f(x) = λe^(−λx) for x ≥ 0 has mean 1/λ, and it is memoryless: P(X > s + t ∣ X > s) = P(X > t).

topics.title: The Poisson Process
topics.short: For random arrivals at rate λ, the count in a window of length t is Poisson with mean λt, and the gaps between arrivals are exponential with mean 1/λ.

topics.title: Densities of Functions of a Variable
topics.short: Find the density of Y = g(X) through its CDF: work out F_Y(y) = P(g(X) ≤ y), then differentiate.

topics.title: Joint and Marginal Distributions
topics.short: A joint table gives P(X = x, Y = y); add across a row or down a column to get the marginal distributions.

topics.title: Conditional Distributions and Independent Variables
topics.short: P(X = x ∣ Y = y) divides a row of the joint table by the row's total; X and Y are independent when every cell equals the product of its marginals.

topics.title: Uniform Points and Geometric Probability
topics.short: When a point is uniform in a region, probability is area over total area: two numbers chosen uniformly from [0, 1] differ by less than 1/4 with probability 7/16.

topics.title: Joint Densities
topics.short: P((X, Y) ∈ R) = ∬_R f(x, y) dA; set up the limits for regions such as {x < y}.

topics.title: Marginal and Conditional Densities
topics.short: f_X(x) = ∫ f(x, y) dy, and X and Y are independent when f(x, y) = f_X(x) f_Y(y) everywhere.

topics.title: Covariance and Correlation
topics.short: Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] − E[X]E[Y], and the correlation ρ = Cov(X, Y)/(σ_X σ_Y) lies between −1 and 1.

topics.title: Variance of a Sum
topics.short: Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2 Cov(X, Y), and the variance of a longer sum adds every pairwise covariance.

topics.title: Sums of Independent Variables
topics.short: The distribution of X + Y comes from adding over every split: P(X + Y = s) = Σ P(X = k) P(Y = s − k), with an integral for densities.

topics.title: Conditional Expectation
topics.short: E[X ∣ Y = y] averages X within one slice, and E[X] = E[E[X ∣ Y]] averages the slices.

topics.title: Maximum and Minimum of Independent Variables
topics.short: P(max ≤ x) = F(x)ⁿ and P(min > x) = (1 − F(x))ⁿ; the minimum of independent exponential variables is exponential with the rates added.

topics.title: Markov's and Chebyshev's Inequalities
topics.short: For X ≥ 0, P(X ≥ a) ≤ E[X]/a; for any X with mean μ and standard deviation σ, P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k².

topics.title: The Law of Large Numbers
topics.short: The average of n independent trials has variance σ²/n, so it settles near μ as n grows.

topics.title: Moment Generating Functions
topics.short: M(t) = E[e^(tX)]; its derivatives at t = 0 give E[X], E[X²], …, and the MGF of a sum of independent variables is the product of their MGFs.

topics.title: The Central Limit Theorem for Sums
topics.short: A sum of n independent copies of X is close to normal, with mean nμ and standard deviation σ√n.

topics.title: The Normal Approximation to the Binomial
topics.short: Approximate Binomial(n, p) with a normal curve, widening each whole number to an interval of width 1: P(X ≤ 12) ≈ P(Y < 12.5).

topics.title: Markov Chains and Transition Matrices
topics.short: The next state depends only on the current one; a row of probabilities times the transition matrix P steps forward, so after n steps the distribution is π₀Pⁿ.

topics.title: Absorption and First-Step Analysis
topics.short: Condition on the first step to get equations for the chance of absorption and the expected time to get there, as in the gambler's ruin.

topics.title: Stationary Distributions
topics.short: Solve πP = π together with π₁ + ⋯ + πₙ = 1 to find the long-run share of time spent in each state.

topics.title: Absolute Value and the Triangle Inequality
topics.short: |x − a| < ε means x is within ε of a; |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| and |a| − |b| ≤ |a − b| turn distances into bounds.

topics.title: Supremum and Infimum
topics.short: The supremum of a set is its least upper bound and the infimum its greatest lower bound; neither has to belong to the set.

topics.title: The ε-Test for a Supremum
topics.short: An upper bound s is the supremum exactly when, for every ε > 0, some element of the set is bigger than s − ε.

topics.title: Completeness and the Archimedean Property
topics.short: Every nonempty set of reals that is bounded above has a supremum; from it, for every ε > 0 some whole number n has 1/n < ε.

topics.title: Density of the Rationals
topics.short: Between any two real numbers a < b lies a rational: pick n with 1/n < b − a, and some multiple m/n lands strictly between them.

topics.title: Countable and Uncountable Sets
topics.short: A set is countable when its elements can be listed a₁, a₂, a₃, …; the rationals are countable, but Cantor's diagonal argument shows the reals are not.

topics.title: The Definition of a Limit (ε–N)
topics.short: aₙ → L when for every ε > 0 there is an N with |aₙ − L| < ε for all n ≥ N; for a given ε you can find such an N and check it.

topics.title: Writing ε–N Proofs
topics.short: Work backward on scratch paper to find N in terms of ε; then write the proof forward: let ε > 0, choose N, take n ≥ N and show |aₙ − L| < ε.

topics.title: Bounded Sequences and Divergence
topics.short: Every convergent sequence is bounded; to show aₙ does not converge to L, find one ε > 0 for which no N works.

topics.title: Proving the Limit Laws
topics.short: If aₙ → a and bₙ → b, then aₙ + bₙ → a + b and aₙbₙ → ab; the proofs split ε between the two pieces and use that convergent sequences are bounded.

topics.title: Order Limits and the Squeeze Theorem
topics.short: Limits keep ≤: if aₙ ≤ bₙ then lim aₙ ≤ lim bₙ; and a sequence trapped between two sequences with the same limit has that limit too.

topics.title: The Monotone Convergence Theorem
topics.short: A bounded monotone sequence converges, to the supremum of its terms if it increases; for aₙ₊₁ = g(aₙ), show monotone and bounded, then solve L = g(L).

topics.title: Subsequences and Subsequential Limits
topics.short: Every subsequence of a convergent sequence has the same limit, so two subsequences with different limits prove that a sequence diverges.

topics.title: The Bolzano–Weierstrass Theorem
topics.short: Every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence: halve the interval again and again, each time keeping a half that holds infinitely many terms.

topics.title: Limit Superior and Limit Inferior
topics.short: lim sup aₙ is the limit of the tail suprema sup{aₖ : k ≥ n}; it is the largest subsequential limit, and aₙ converges exactly when lim sup aₙ = lim inf aₙ.

topics.title: Cauchy Sequences
topics.short: aₙ is Cauchy when for every ε > 0 some N makes |aₘ − aₙ| < ε for all m, n ≥ N; in ℝ a sequence is Cauchy exactly when it converges.

topics.title: Series and the Cauchy Criterion
topics.short: ∑aₖ converges when its partial sums do; by the Cauchy criterion, blocks aₘ₊₁ + ⋯ + aₙ far out must be small, and in particular aₖ → 0.

topics.title: Comparison and Absolute Convergence
topics.short: If |aₖ| ≤ bₖ and ∑bₖ converges, the Cauchy criterion makes ∑aₖ converge; in particular, absolute convergence implies convergence.

topics.title: The Cauchy Condensation Test
topics.short: For a decreasing sequence of positive terms, ∑aₙ and ∑2ᵏa₂ₖ converge or diverge together; it settles the p-series and ∑1/(n(ln n)ᵖ).

topics.title: Root and Ratio Tests with lim sup
topics.short: If lim sup |aₖ|^(1/k) < 1 the series converges absolutely, and if it is > 1 the series diverges; the root test works even when the ratios jump around.

topics.title: Alternating Series and Error Bounds
topics.short: If bₖ decreases to 0, ∑(−1)ᵏ⁺¹bₖ converges, and the error after n terms is less than bₙ₊₁: the partial sums zigzag and trap the sum.

topics.title: Rearranging Series
topics.short: Rearranging an absolutely convergent series keeps its sum; a conditionally convergent series can be rearranged to add up to any number you like (Riemann).

topics.title: Limits of Functions (ε–δ)
topics.short: lim f(x) = L as x → a when for every ε > 0 some δ > 0 gives |f(x) − L| < ε whenever 0 < |x − a| < δ; any smaller positive δ works too.

topics.title: Continuity with ε and δ
topics.short: f is continuous at a when for every ε > 0 some δ > 0 gives |f(x) − f(a)| < ε whenever |x − a| < δ; for x² the classic choice is δ = min(1, ε/(2|a| + 1)).

topics.title: The Sequential Criterion and Discontinuity
topics.short: f is continuous at a exactly when f(xₙ) → f(a) for every sequence xₙ → a; two sequences giving different limits prove a discontinuity.

topics.title: The Intermediate Value Theorem
topics.short: A continuous function on [a, b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b); the proof uses c = sup{x : f(x) < 0}, and bisection traps c to any accuracy.

topics.title: The Extreme Value Theorem
topics.short: A continuous function on a closed, bounded interval attains a maximum and a minimum; drop any hypothesis and the supremum may not be attained.

topics.title: Uniform Continuity
topics.short: f is uniformly continuous on S when one δ works for every point of S at once; continuous functions on [a, b] are, but 1/x on (0, 1) is not.

topics.title: Derivatives from the Definition
topics.short: f′(a) = lim (f(a + h) − f(a))/h as h → 0; the definition handles what the rules can't, like x² sin(1/x) at 0.

topics.title: Differentiability and Continuity
topics.short: Differentiable at a implies continuous at a, but not conversely; at a break point the one-sided derivatives must exist and agree.

topics.title: Rolle's Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem
topics.short: If f is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), some c in (a, b) has f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a); Rolle's theorem is the case f(a) = f(b).

topics.title: Inequalities from the Mean Value Theorem
topics.short: If |f′| ≤ K on an interval, then |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ K|x − y| there; this proves bounds like |sin x − sin y| ≤ |x − y| and gives δ = ε/K.

topics.title: Taylor's Theorem with Remainder
topics.short: f(x) = Pₙ(x) + f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(c)(x − a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1)! for some c between a and x; a bound on f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾ bounds the error.

topics.title: Upper and Lower Sums
topics.short: For a partition P, U(f, P) uses the supremum of f on each piece and L(f, P) the infimum; every lower sum is at most every upper sum, and refining P brings them together.

topics.title: The Integrability Criterion
topics.short: f is integrable exactly when for every ε > 0 some partition has U(f, P) − L(f, P) < ε; for monotone f on n equal pieces the gap is |f(b) − f(a)|(b − a)/n.

topics.title: Which Functions Are Integrable
topics.short: Continuous functions, monotone functions and bounded functions with finitely many jumps are integrable; Dirichlet's function is not, since every U = b − a and every L = 0.

topics.title: Bounds and the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
topics.short: If m ≤ f ≤ M on [a, b], then m(b − a) ≤ ∫f ≤ M(b − a); a continuous f equals its average value at some c in [a, b].

topics.title: Proving the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
topics.short: F(x) = ∫ₐˣ f is continuous, and F′(c) = f(c) wherever f is continuous; at a jump of f, F has a corner.

topics.title: Limits of Sums as Integrals
topics.short: Because continuous functions are integrable, every Riemann sum tends to the integral; so a limit like (1/n)∑f(k/n) is ∫₀¹ f(x) dx.

topics.title: Pointwise Convergence
topics.short: fₙ → f pointwise when fₙ(x) → f(x) at each x separately; a pointwise limit of continuous functions can jump, as xⁿ on [0, 1] does.

topics.title: Uniform Convergence and the Sup Norm
topics.short: fₙ → f uniformly when ‖fₙ − f‖ = sup |fₙ(x) − f(x)| → 0: one N works for every x at once.

topics.title: What Uniform Convergence Keeps
topics.short: A uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, and ∫fₙ → ∫f; without uniform convergence, the limit of the integrals can differ from the integral of the limit.

topics.title: The Weierstrass M-Test
topics.short: If |fₖ(x)| ≤ Mₖ for every x and ∑Mₖ converges, then ∑fₖ converges uniformly (and absolutely).

topics.title: Power Series: Radius and Uniform Convergence
topics.short: ∑cₙxⁿ has radius R = 1/lim sup |cₙ|^(1/n); it converges uniformly on every [−r, r] with r < R, so its sum is continuous inside the interval.

topics.title: Metric Spaces
topics.short: A metric d measures distance: d(x, y) > 0 unless x = y, d(x, y) = d(y, x), and d(x, z) ≤ d(x, y) + d(y, z); the taxicab, Euclidean and max metrics on ℝ² are three examples.

topics.title: Open and Closed Sets
topics.short: A set is open when every point has a ball around it inside the set, and closed when it contains all its limit points; the closure adds the limit points.

topics.title: Compact Sets
topics.short: K is compact when every open cover has a finite subcover; in ℝⁿ that happens exactly when K is closed and bounded (Heine–Borel).

topics.title: The Contraction Mapping Theorem
topics.short: If d(g(x), g(y)) ≤ k·d(x, y) with k < 1 on a complete space, g has exactly one fixed point, and the nth iterate is within kⁿd(x₁, x₀)/(1 − k) of it.

topics.title: Categorical and Quantitative Variables
topics.short: Tell whether data are labels or measured numbers.

topics.title: Displaying Categorical Data
topics.short: Read bar graphs, pie charts and relative frequencies.

topics.title: Histograms and Shape
topics.short: Describe shape as symmetric, skewed, unimodal or bimodal.

topics.title: Mean, Median and Resistance
topics.short: The median resists outliers; the mean does not.

topics.title: Standard Deviation
topics.short: A typical distance from the mean.

topics.title: Five-Number Summary and Outliers
topics.short: Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to flag outliers.

topics.title: Comparing Distributions
topics.short: Compare shape, center and spread in context.

topics.title: z-Scores and Percentiles
topics.short: z tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean.

topics.title: Shifting and Scaling Data
topics.short: Adding a constant moves the center; multiplying scales center and spread.

topics.title: The Normal Curve and the 68-95-99.7 Rule
topics.short: About 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations.

topics.title: Areas under the Normal Curve
topics.short: Find the proportion below, above or between values.

topics.title: Finding Values from Percentiles
topics.short: Work backward from an area to a z-score to a value.

topics.title: Describing Scatterplots
topics.short: Describe direction, form, strength and unusual points.

topics.title: The Correlation Coefficient
topics.short: r measures the direction and strength of a linear pattern.

topics.title: The Least-Squares Regression Line
topics.short: The line that makes the sum of squared residuals smallest.

topics.title: Interpreting Slope and Intercept
topics.short: Say what the slope and intercept mean in context, with units.

topics.title: Residuals and Residual Plots
topics.short: A good linear fit leaves residuals with no pattern.

topics.title: r² and the Quality of Fit
topics.short: r² is the fraction of the variation in y explained by the line.

topics.title: Outliers and Influential Points
topics.short: Some points pull the line toward themselves.

topics.title: Fitting Exponential and Power Models
topics.short: Use logs to straighten curved data.

topics.title: Correlation, Causation and Lurking Variables
topics.short: Association alone does not show cause and effect.

topics.title: Sampling Methods
topics.short: Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic samples.

topics.title: Bias in Sampling and Surveys
topics.short: Spot undercoverage, nonresponse and leading questions.

topics.title: Observational Studies and Experiments
topics.short: Only a randomized experiment can show cause and effect.

topics.title: Designing Experiments
topics.short: Use control, random assignment, replication and blocking.

topics.title: Evaluating Statistical Reports
topics.short: Judge claims in the news by how the data were produced.

topics.title: Events, Unions, Intersections and Complements
topics.short: Describe events with "or," "and" and "not."

topics.title: The Addition Rule
topics.short: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

topics.title: Conditional Probability
topics.short: P(A ∣ B) is the probability of A among the outcomes where B happened.

topics.title: Conditional Probability from Two-Way Tables
topics.short: Divide by the row or column total that matches the condition.

topics.title: Independent Events
topics.short: A and B are independent when P(A ∣ B) = P(A).

topics.title: The General Multiplication Rule
topics.short: P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B ∣ A).

topics.title: Bayes' Rule
topics.short: Reverse a conditional probability with a tree or a table.

topics.title: Permutations
topics.short: Count arrangements when order matters.

topics.title: Combinations
topics.short: Count selections when order does not matter.

topics.title: Probability with Counting
topics.short: Use permutations and combinations to find probabilities.

topics.title: Discrete Random Variables
topics.short: List values and their probabilities in a table.

topics.title: Expected Value
topics.short: The long-run average outcome: Σ x · P(x).

topics.title: Standard Deviation of a Random Variable
topics.short: Measure how much a random variable typically varies from its mean.

topics.title: Sums and Differences of Random Variables
topics.short: Means add; for independent variables, variances add.

topics.title: The Binomial Distribution
topics.short: Count successes in n independent trials with the same p.

topics.title: The Geometric Distribution
topics.short: Count the trials until the first success.

topics.title: Continuous Random Variables
topics.short: Probability is area under a density curve.

topics.title: Decisions with Expected Value
topics.short: Compare games, insurance and strategies by expected payoff.

topics.title: Is the Model Consistent? Simulation
topics.short: Use simulation to judge whether data fit a model.

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of a Proportion
topics.short: Sample proportions center on p with spread √(p(1 − p)/n).

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of a Mean and the CLT
topics.short: Sample means are close to normal for large n, with spread σ/√n.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for a Proportion
topics.short: Estimate ± margin of error.

topics.title: Margin of Error and Sample Size
topics.short: Quadrupling the sample size halves the margin of error.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for a Mean
topics.short: Use t when the population standard deviation is unknown.

topics.title: The Logic of Significance Tests
topics.short: Ask how surprising the data would be if the null hypothesis were true.

topics.title: Testing a Claim about a Proportion
topics.short: Carry out a one-proportion z test.

topics.title: Testing a Claim about a Mean
topics.short: Carry out a one-sample t test.

topics.title: Type I and Type II Errors and Power
topics.short: Weigh the two kinds of mistakes a test can make.

topics.title: Comparing Two Treatments by Randomization
topics.short: Reshuffle groups to see whether a difference could be chance.

topics.title: Two-Sample Intervals and Tests
topics.short: Compare two proportions or two means.

topics.title: Chi-Square Tests
topics.short: Test goodness of fit and association in two-way tables.

topics.title: Inference for the Slope of a Regression Line
topics.short: Test and estimate the true slope from sample data.

topics.title: The Celestial Sphere
topics.short: The sky looks like a dome that turns once a day around the celestial poles, because Earth spins.

topics.title: Altitude, Azimuth and Your Latitude
topics.short: The North Star's altitude equals your latitude, and stars close enough to the pole never set.

topics.title: Right Ascension and Declination
topics.short: Declination and right ascension are the sky's latitude and longitude, fixed to the stars.

topics.title: Solar and Sidereal Days
topics.short: Earth spins once in 23 h 56 min, but noon to noon takes 24 h because Earth also moves along its orbit.

topics.title: The Sun's Path Through the Year
topics.short: The Sun's declination swings between +23.4° and −23.4°, which sets the solstices, the equinoxes, the tropics and the polar circles.

topics.title: The Sun's Noon Altitude
topics.short: The Sun's altitude at noon is 90° − latitude + the Sun's declination.

topics.title: Moon Phases and Moonrise Times
topics.short: Each phase rises at its own time: a full Moon rises at sunset and a first-quarter Moon about noon, because of where the Moon sits relative to the Sun.

topics.title: Synodic and Sidereal Months
topics.short: The phases repeat every 29.5 days, longer than the Moon's 27.3-day orbit, because Earth moves along its orbit too.

topics.title: Eclipse Seasons
topics.short: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5°, so eclipses happen only near the two nodes, in eclipse seasons about six months apart.

topics.title: From an Earth-Centered to a Sun-Centered Sky
topics.short: Retrograde loops and the phases of Venus favor Copernicus's Sun-centered model.

topics.title: Kepler's First Law: Ellipses
topics.short: Planets move on ellipses with the Sun at one focus, and eccentricity measures how stretched each one is.

topics.title: Kepler's Second Law: Equal Areas
topics.short: A planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times, so it moves fastest when nearest the Sun.

topics.title: Kepler's Third Law
topics.short: P² = a³ when the period is in years and the size of the orbit is in astronomical units.

topics.title: Weighing Stars and Planets with Orbits
topics.short: Newton's form of Kepler's third law, M = a³/P² in solar masses, AU and years, gives the mass at the center.

topics.title: Orbital Speed and Escape Speed
topics.short: A low circular orbit needs about 7.9 km/s at Earth, and escaping takes √2 times the circular speed.

topics.title: Spring and Neap Tides
topics.short: When the Sun and Moon line up, their tides add to make spring tides; at the quarter Moons they partly cancel, making neap tides.

topics.title: Looking Back in Time
topics.short: Light takes time to reach us (8.3 minutes from the Sun), so the farther we look, the older the view.

topics.title: Color and Temperature: Wien's Law
