topics.short: Hotter objects glow bluer: the peak wavelength is λ_peak = 2.9 × 10⁶ nm·K ÷ T.

topics.title: Luminosity, Size and Temperature
topics.short: A star's power is L = 4πR²σT⁴, so in solar units L = R²T⁴.

topics.title: Spectral Lines and Kirchhoff's Laws
topics.short: Hot, dense objects give a continuous spectrum; thin gases give bright lines or, in front of a hotter source, dark lines.

topics.title: The Doppler Shift of Light
topics.short: A spectral line's shift gives the speed toward or away from us: Δλ/λ = v/c.

topics.title: Telescopes: Light-Gathering and Resolution
topics.short: A telescope's light-gathering power grows with the square of its diameter, and a bigger aperture shows finer detail.

topics.title: Observing Across the Spectrum
topics.short: Radio, infrared, X-ray and gamma-ray telescopes see what eyes can't, and some must fly above the air.

topics.title: Planet Densities: Rock or Gas?
topics.short: A planet's mass and radius give its average density, about 4 to 5.5 g/cm³ for rocky planets and 0.7 to 1.6 g/cm³ for the giants.

topics.title: How the Solar System Formed
topics.short: A spinning cloud flattened into a disk; rock and metal condensed near the Sun and ices farther out.

topics.title: Comets and Meteor Showers
topics.short: Comets on long, stretched orbits grow tails that point away from the Sun, and Earth passing through their dust makes meteor showers.

topics.title: Finding Planets Around Other Stars
topics.short: A passing planet dims its star by (R_planet/R_star)², and a planet's tug makes its star wobble.

topics.title: Layers of the Sun
topics.short: Energy made in the core moves out through the radiative and convective zones to the glowing photosphere.

topics.title: How the Sun Shines
topics.short: Fusing hydrogen into helium turns about 0.7% of the mass into energy, by E = mc².

topics.title: The Sun's Lifetime
topics.short: Fuel divided by the rate of use gives the Sun about 10 billion years on the main sequence.

topics.title: Sunspots and the Solar Cycle
topics.short: Magnetic fields make cooler, darker sunspots, and solar activity rises and falls about every 11 years.

topics.title: Parallax and the Parsec
topics.short: A star's distance in parsecs is 1 divided by its parallax angle in arcseconds.

topics.title: Brightness and Distance
topics.short: Apparent brightness falls off with the square of the distance: b = L/(4πd²).

topics.title: The Magnitude Scale
topics.short: Smaller magnitudes are brighter, and 5 magnitudes means 100 times the brightness.

topics.title: Spectral Classes
topics.short: The classes O, B, A, F, G, K and M sort stars from hottest to coolest by their spectral lines.

topics.title: The H–R Diagram
topics.short: Plot luminosity against temperature to sort stars into the main sequence, giants and white dwarfs.

topics.title: Binary Stars and Stellar Masses
topics.short: Two stars orbiting each other reveal their masses, and the main sequence turns out to be a sequence of mass.

topics.title: How Stars Are Born
topics.short: Gravity pulls cold clouds of gas and dust into protostars until their cores are hot enough for fusion.

topics.title: Main-Sequence Lifetimes
topics.short: A star's lifetime goes as its fuel over its luminosity, about M^(−2.5), so massive stars die young.

topics.title: Red Giants and White Dwarfs
topics.short: When core hydrogen runs out a star swells into a red giant; a Sun-like star ends as an Earth-sized white dwarf.

topics.title: Reading a Cluster's Age
topics.short: All stars in a cluster were born together, so the point where the main sequence ends gives its age.

topics.title: Supernovae and the Elements
topics.short: Massive stars fuse elements up to iron, then their cores collapse and explode, spreading heavy elements into space.

topics.title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars
topics.short: A collapsed core can become a city-sized ball of neutrons spinning many times a second.

topics.title: Black Holes
topics.short: Within the event horizon, R = 2GM/c², not even light can escape, yet far away a black hole pulls like any other mass.

topics.title: The Milky Way
topics.short: Our galaxy is a disk of a few hundred billion stars, with the Sun about 26,000 light-years from the center.

topics.title: Kinds of Galaxies
topics.short: Spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies differ in shape, gas and the ages of their stars.

topics.title: Dark Matter
topics.short: Stars and gas far out in galaxies orbit too fast for the mass we can see, so most of a galaxy's mass is dark.

topics.title: Standard Candles
topics.short: Cepheid variables and type Ia supernovae have known luminosities, so how bright they look tells how far away they are.

topics.title: Hubble's Law
topics.short: Distant galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance: v = H₀d.

topics.title: The Age of the Universe
topics.short: Running the expansion backward, 1/H₀ gives an age of about 14 billion years.

topics.title: Evidence for the Big Bang
topics.short: The expansion, the cosmic microwave background and the amounts of hydrogen and helium all point to a hot, dense early universe.

topics.title: The Accelerating Universe
topics.short: Distant supernovae show the expansion is speeding up, and we call the unknown cause dark energy.

topics.title: Magnitude Arithmetic
topics.short: Magnitudes compare fluxes on a log scale: m₁ − m₂ = −2.5 log(F₁/F₂).

topics.title: Absolute Magnitude and the Distance Modulus
topics.short: A star's absolute magnitude is its magnitude seen from 10 pc, and m − M = 5 log(d/10 pc).

topics.title: Interstellar Dust: Extinction and Reddening
topics.short: Dust dims and reddens starlight, adding A to the distance modulus: m − M = 5 log(d/10 pc) + A.

topics.title: Color Index and Temperature
topics.short: The color index B − V compares two magnitudes, and a smaller value means a hotter star.

topics.title: The Planck Function
topics.short: B_λ(T) gives a blackbody's spectrum; its peak gives Wien's law and its area gives σT⁴.

topics.title: Effective Temperature and Stellar Radii
topics.short: Use L = 4πR²σT_eff⁴ with real values to find the radii of dwarfs, giants and supergiants.

topics.title: Excitation and the Strength of Spectral Lines
topics.short: The fraction of atoms in an excited level follows (g_b/g_a)e^(−ΔE/kT), which is why hydrogen lines peak in A stars.

topics.title: Ionization and the Spectral Sequence
topics.short: Rising temperature ionizes each element in turn, so the spectral classes are a temperature sequence, not a sequence of composition.

topics.title: Masses from Visual Binaries
topics.short: Parallax turns angular separation into a, Kepler's third law gives M₁ + M₂, and the center of mass splits it.

topics.title: Spectroscopic Binaries
topics.short: Doppler shifts trace each star's orbit, and their speeds give the mass ratio m₁/m₂ = v₂/v₁.

topics.title: Eclipsing Binaries
topics.short: The timing of eclipses gives the stars' radii, and the depths compare their surface temperatures.

topics.title: Exoplanet Transits
topics.short: A transit's depth (R_p/R_*)² gives the planet's size, and its period gives the orbit.

topics.title: Exoplanet Masses from Wobbles
topics.short: A planet's pull sets its star's velocity amplitude, which gives the planet's mass times sin i.

topics.title: Planet Temperatures and the Habitable Zone
topics.short: Balancing absorbed starlight against emitted heat gives T = T_*(1 − A)^(1/4)√(R_*/(2d)).

topics.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium
topics.short: In a star, pressure balances gravity layer by layer: dP/dr = −Gm(r)ρ/r².

topics.title: Estimating a Star's Center
topics.short: Order-of-magnitude estimates give P_c ~ GM²/R⁴ and T_c ~ GMm_p/(kR), millions of kelvins for the Sun.

topics.title: The Virial Theorem
topics.short: For a gas ball held by its own gravity, 2K + U = 0, so losing energy makes it contract and heat up.

topics.title: Gravity as a Power Source
topics.short: Contraction alone could power the Sun for only the Kelvin–Helmholtz time GM²/(RL), about 30 million years.

topics.title: The Proton–Proton Chain and the CNO Cycle
topics.short: Four protons become helium-4 and release 26.7 MeV; the CNO cycle takes over in hotter, heavier stars.

topics.title: Why Fusion Needs Tunneling
topics.short: The Coulomb barrier is far higher than kT in the Sun's core, so protons fuse only by tunneling.

topics.title: Radiation and Convection Inside Stars
topics.short: Photons random-walk outward, so N steps of length ℓ cover only √N·ℓ, and the trip out of the Sun takes on the order of 100,000 years.

topics.title: The Mass–Luminosity Relation
topics.short: On the main sequence L ∝ M^3.5 roughly, so lifetimes go as M^(−2.5).

topics.title: The Eddington Luminosity
topics.short: Radiation pressure on electrons balances gravity at L_Edd ≈ 3.3 × 10⁴ (M/M_⊙) L_⊙.

topics.title: Solar Neutrinos
topics.short: Neutrinos leave the core at once, letting us see fusion directly, and their changing flavors solved the solar neutrino problem.

topics.title: Evolutionary Tracks
topics.short: A star's path across the H–R diagram follows the changes in its core.

topics.title: Electron Degeneracy Pressure
topics.short: The exclusion principle makes packed electrons push back even when they are cold.

topics.title: The White Dwarf Mass–Radius Relation
topics.short: Degeneracy gives R ∝ M^(−1/3), so heavier white dwarfs are smaller.

topics.title: The Chandrasekhar Limit
topics.short: Electrons moving near light speed can hold up at most about 1.4 solar masses.

topics.title: Core-Collapse Supernovae
topics.short: An iron core collapses in under a second, and neutrinos carry off about 10⁴⁶ J.

topics.title: Neutron Stars
topics.short: A collapsing core keeps its angular momentum and magnetic flux, so neutron stars spin fast with huge fields.

topics.title: Pulsar Spin-Down
topics.short: A pulsar's lost rotational energy, dE/dt = Iωω̇, powers the nebula around it.

topics.title: The Schwarzschild Radius
topics.short: r_s = 2GM/c², about 3 km for each solar mass.

topics.title: Gravitational Redshift and Time Dilation
topics.short: A clock at radius r runs slow by √(1 − r_s/r) compared with one far away.

topics.title: Tidal Forces and the Roche Limit
topics.short: The difference in gravity across a body, about 2GMmΔr/r³, tears apart moons and stretches matter near black holes.

topics.title: Accretion Power
topics.short: Matter falling onto a compact object releases about GMṁ/R, far more per kilogram than fusion near a neutron star.

topics.title: Gravitational Waves
topics.short: Orbiting compact objects radiate gravitational waves and spiral inward; LIGO first detected merging black holes in 2015.

topics.title: Rotation Curves and Dark Matter
topics.short: v(r) = √(GM(r)/r), so a flat rotation curve needs mass that grows in proportion to r.

topics.title: Supermassive Black Holes
topics.short: Stars orbiting the center of the Milky Way weigh its black hole at about 4 million suns.

topics.title: The Cosmic Distance Ladder
topics.short: Parallax calibrates Cepheids, Cepheids calibrate type Ia supernovae, and each rung reaches farther.

topics.title: Redshift and the Scale Factor
topics.short: 1 + z = λ_observed/λ_emitted = a(now)/a(then): light stretches as space expands.

topics.title: Hubble's Law in Practice
topics.short: For small z, d ≈ cz/H₀, and 1/H₀ sets the age scale of the universe.

topics.title: The Friedmann Equation and Critical Density
topics.short: H² = 8πGρ/3 − kc²/a², so a flat universe has the critical density 3H²/(8πG).

topics.title: Matter, Radiation and Dark Energy Through Time
topics.short: Matter thins as a⁻³, radiation as a⁻⁴, and dark energy stays constant, so each ruled in turn.

topics.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background
topics.short: The background's temperature scales as 1/a: 2.725 K today, about 3000 K when atoms formed.

topics.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
topics.short: In its first minutes the universe made about 25% helium by mass, matching what we measure.

topics.title: Charge Densities
topics.short: λ, σ and ρ describe charge spread along a line, over a surface or through a volume, so dq = λ dx.

topics.title: The Field of a Charged Rod
topics.short: Add up dE = k dq/r² as components to find the field of a charged rod.

topics.title: Fields of a Ring and a Disk
topics.short: On the axis of a ring E = kQz/(z² + R²)^(3/2), and a disk is built from rings.

topics.title: Electric Flux
topics.short: Φ_E = ∫E · dA counts the field passing through a surface, using the surface's normal.

topics.title: Gauss's Law
topics.short: The total flux through any closed surface equals q_enclosed/ε₀.

topics.title: Gauss's Law with Spherical Symmetry
topics.short: Find the fields of point charges, charged shells and uniformly charged balls, inside and out.

topics.title: Gauss's Law for Lines and Planes
topics.short: A long line gives E = λ/(2πε₀r) and a large sheet gives E = σ/(2ε₀), the same at every distance.

topics.title: Conductors in Electrostatic Equilibrium
topics.short: Inside a conductor E = 0, excess charge sits on the surface, and just outside E = σ/ε₀.

topics.title: Potential from the Field
topics.short: ΔV = −∫E · dl, so potential falls along the direction of the field.

topics.title: Potentials of Charge Distributions
topics.short: V = k∫dq/r adds up as a scalar for rods, rings and disks.

topics.title: Field from Potential
topics.short: E = −dV/dr, and in three dimensions E = −(∂V/∂x, ∂V/∂y, ∂V/∂z).

topics.title: Energy of a System of Charges
topics.short: Add kqᵢqⱼ/rᵢⱼ over every pair to find the energy needed to assemble the charges.

topics.title: Energy Conservation for Moving Charges
topics.short: A charge released near fixed charges trades potential energy for kinetic energy: qΔV + ΔK = 0.

topics.title: Connecting Conductors
topics.short: Connected conductors come to the same potential, so two spheres share charge in proportion to their radii.

topics.title: Capacitance from Geometry
topics.short: Find C with Gauss's law and ΔV for parallel-plate, cylindrical and spherical capacitors.

topics.title: Energy Stored in the Electric Field
topics.short: The energy of a charged capacitor lives in its field, with density u = ½ε₀E².

topics.title: Dielectrics
topics.short: A dielectric weakens the field by κ and raises C to κC; with the battery connected Q grows, but disconnected V drops.

topics.title: Current Density and Drift Velocity
topics.short: I = nqv_dA and J = I/A; electrons drift along at a fraction of a millimeter per second, even though a signal travels nearly at light speed.

topics.title: Resistance of Tapered Conductors
topics.short: Add dR = ρ dx/A(x) along a conductor whose cross section changes.

topics.title: Multi-Loop Circuits
topics.short: Write junction and loop equations and solve them as a system.

topics.title: Charging a Capacitor
topics.short: The loop rule gives a differential equation whose solution is q = Cε(1 − e^(−t/RC)).

topics.title: Discharging and Energy in RC Circuits
topics.short: A capacitor discharges as q = Q₀e^(−t/RC), and all of its stored energy ends up as heat in the resistor.

topics.title: The Lorentz Force
topics.short: F = q(E + v × B), computed with cross products.

topics.title: Velocity Selectors and Mass Spectrometers
topics.short: Only charges with v = E/B pass straight through crossed fields, and the radius of the path then sorts them by mass-to-charge ratio.

topics.title: The Hall Effect
topics.short: A current crossing a magnetic field pushes its carriers sideways, building a voltage that reveals their sign.

topics.title: Force on a Current-Carrying Wire
topics.short: dF = I dl × B, integrated along bent wires.

topics.title: Torque on a Current Loop
topics.short: A loop has magnetic moment μ = NIA, and τ = μ × B turns motors and meters.

topics.title: The Biot–Savart Law
topics.short: Each piece of current makes dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r².

topics.title: Fields of Loops and Arcs
topics.short: At the center of a loop B = μ₀I/(2R), and on the axis the field falls off with distance.

topics.title: Ampère's Law
topics.short: ∮B · dl = μ₀I_enclosed around any closed path.

topics.title: Fields Inside Wires, Solenoids and Toroids
topics.short: Ampère's law gives B = μ₀Ir/(2πR²) inside a wire, μ₀nI in a solenoid and μ₀NI/(2πr) in a toroid.

topics.title: Magnetic Flux That Changes
topics.short: Φ = ∫B · dA can change because B, the area or the angle changes with time.

topics.title: Faraday's Law with Calculus
topics.short: ε = −dΦ/dt for loops that rotate, grow or sit in changing fields.

topics.title: Generators
topics.short: A coil of N turns spinning at ω in a field B makes ε = NBAω sin ωt.

topics.title: Induced Electric Fields
topics.short: A changing magnetic field makes a curling electric field: ∮E · dl = −dΦ/dt, with or without a wire.

topics.title: Induced Currents and Magnetic Forces
topics.short: The force on an induced current opposes the motion, so a rod on rails coasts to a stop or falls at a terminal speed.

topics.title: Self-Inductance
topics.short: ε = −L dI/dt, and a long solenoid has L = μ₀N²A/ℓ.

topics.title: Mutual Inductance and Transformers
topics.short: A changing current in one coil induces an emf in another, so a transformer gives V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p.

topics.title: RL Circuits
topics.short: The current rises as I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−Rt/L)), with time constant L/R.

topics.title: Energy in Inductors and Magnetic Fields
topics.short: An inductor stores U = ½LI², with field energy density u = B²/(2μ₀).

topics.title: LC Oscillations
topics.short: Energy sloshes between the capacitor and the inductor at ω = 1/√(LC), like a mass on a spring.

topics.title: RLC Circuits
topics.short: Resistance damps LC oscillations, just as friction damps a mass on a spring.

topics.title: Alternating Current and RMS Values
topics.short: V = V₀ sin ωt, and the rms value V₀/√2 gives the same average power as a steady voltage.

topics.title: Reactance of Capacitors and Inductors
topics.short: X_C = 1/(ωC) and X_L = ωL; current leads the voltage in a capacitor and lags it in an inductor.

topics.title: Impedance and Phasors
topics.short: In a series RLC circuit Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R.

topics.title: Resonance and Power in AC Circuits
topics.short: At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the current peaks, and the average power is I_rms·V_rms·cos φ.

topics.title: Displacement Current
topics.short: A changing electric field acts like a current in Ampère's law, which fills the gap of a charging capacitor.

topics.title: Maxwell's Equations
topics.short: Four laws in integral form hold all of electricity and magnetism.

topics.title: Electromagnetic Waves from Maxwell's Equations
topics.short: In empty space the fields travel as a wave at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀), with E = cB.

topics.title: Energy and Momentum of Light
topics.short: Intensity I = ½cε₀E₀² flows along the Poynting vector, and light presses on surfaces with pressure I/c.

topics.title: A Ball Thrown From a Cliff
topics.short: Split the flight into a steady sideways part and a falling part, then use energy for the landing speed.

topics.title: A Kick Over a Wall
topics.short: Find when the ball reaches the wall from the sideways motion, then its height and direction at that moment.

topics.title: A Collision, Then a Ramp
topics.short: Momentum through the collision, energy after it: the carts stick, lose kinetic energy, then climb a ramp.

topics.title: Around a Loop
topics.short: Energy gives the speed at the top of a loop; the circle's force equation gives the push of the track.

topics.title: A Ball Swinging in a Circle
topics.short: A ball on a string sweeps a cone: the tension's vertical part holds it up, its sideways part turns it.

topics.title: A Block on a Spring
topics.short: Period, top speed and timing for a block oscillating on a spring.

topics.title: Down a Rough Ramp Into a Spring
topics.short: Friction takes energy on the ramp; what is left squeezes a spring.

topics.title: Gas Under a Weighted Piston
topics.short: Balance the piston to find the gas pressure, then heat the gas at that pressure.

topics.title: A Gas Engine Cycle
topics.short: Work as the area of a cycle, heat taken in on each leg, and the engine's efficiency.

topics.title: Two Speakers in Step
topics.short: Path difference decides loud or quiet; then find the frequencies that make a spot quiet.

topics.title: A Siren Near a Wall
topics.short: A moving siren, its echo from a wall, and the beats between them.

topics.title: A String Over a Pulley
topics.short: A hanging mass sets the wave speed; the length and the number of loops set the frequency.

topics.title: An Object and a Convex Lens
topics.short: The lens equation, the image's size and kind, and what happens when the object moves.

topics.title: A Lamp at the Bottom of a Pool
topics.short: Snell's law out of the water, the critical angle, and the bright circle on the surface.

topics.title: Light Through Two Slits
topics.short: Fringe spacing, where the bright and dark fringes fall, and how the pattern changes.

topics.title: A Circuit With a Capacitor
topics.short: An uncharged capacitor acts like a wire; a full one passes no current.

topics.title: A Beam Between Charged Plates
topics.short: A charge crossing a uniform field moves like a projectile: steady across, accelerated sideways.

topics.title: A Particle Bent by a Magnetic Field
topics.short: A voltage speeds an ion up; a magnetic field bends it into a half circle that sorts by mass.

topics.title: A Rod Sliding on Rails
topics.short: A moving rod makes an emf, the current feels a force, and someone has to keep pulling.

topics.title: Light on a Metal Plate
topics.short: Photon energy, the fastest electrons and the stopping voltage.

topics.title: Jumps Between Energy Levels
topics.short: Level energies, the photon from a jump, its wavelength and how many lines a gas can give.

topics.title: Velocity as a Derivative
topics.short: v = dx/dt gives the velocity at any instant from the position function.

topics.title: Acceleration as a Derivative
topics.short: a = dv/dt = d²x/dt², and zero velocity at an instant says nothing about the acceleration.

topics.title: Velocity and Position from Acceleration
topics.short: Integrate a(t) once for v(t) and again for x(t), using the starting values to fix the constants.

topics.title: Deriving the Constant-Acceleration Equations
topics.short: Integrating a constant acceleration twice gives the familiar equations and shows exactly when they apply.

topics.title: Acceleration That Depends on Position
topics.short: When a depends on x, write a = v dv/dx and integrate over x.

topics.title: Position, Velocity and Acceleration Vectors
topics.short: r(t), v = dr/dt and a = dv/dt describe motion in two and three dimensions, one component at a time.

topics.title: Projectiles with Calculus
topics.short: Use derivatives to find the highest point, the range and the launch angle that goes farthest.

topics.title: Relative Motion and Galilean Frames
topics.short: Frames moving at constant velocity disagree about velocities but agree about accelerations and forces.

topics.title: Tangential and Centripetal Acceleration
topics.short: On a curve, acceleration splits into dv/dt along the path and v²/r toward the center.

topics.title: Motion Under a Time-Varying Force
topics.short: Integrate F(t)/m to find the velocity when the force changes with time.

topics.title: Linear Drag and Terminal Velocity
topics.short: With drag F = −bv, the speed approaches v_T = mg/b as v(t) = v_T(1 − e^(−t/τ)), with τ = m/b.

topics.title: Quadratic Drag
topics.short: Fast objects in air feel drag ½CρAv², which gives a terminal speed √(2mg/(CρA)).

topics.title: Banked Curves With and Without Friction
topics.short: Find the design speed of a banked road and the range of speeds friction allows.

topics.title: Constraints in Pulley Systems
topics.short: The fixed length of a rope links the accelerations, so a movable pulley gives a₁ = 2a₂.

topics.title: Center of Mass by Integration
topics.short: x_cm = (1/M)∫x dm, with dm = λ dx for a rod whose density varies.

topics.title: Work by a Variable Force
topics.short: W = ∫F dx, the area under the force–position curve.

topics.title: Work Along a Path
topics.short: W = ∫F · dr adds up only the part of the force along each small step of the path.

topics.title: The Work-Energy Theorem from Newton's Second Law
topics.short: Integrating m dv/dt over x turns F = ma into W_net = ΔK.

topics.title: Conservative Forces
topics.short: A force is conservative when its work doesn't depend on the path, so its work around any closed loop is zero.

topics.title: Potential Energy from Force
topics.short: U(x) = −∫F dx, which gives ½kx² for a spring and mgy for uniform gravity.

topics.title: Force from Potential Energy
topics.short: F = −dU/dx: the force points downhill on the potential energy curve.

topics.title: Potential Energy Diagrams
topics.short: Read turning points, allowed regions and stable or unstable equilibria from a graph of U(x).

topics.title: Instantaneous Power
topics.short: P = dW/dt = F · v gives the power at each instant.

topics.title: Gravitational Potential Energy and Escape Speed
topics.short: From U = −GMm/r, the escape speed is √(2GM/r), the same for any mass.

topics.title: Impulse as an Integral
topics.short: J = ∫F dt for any force that changes in time.

topics.title: Solving Elastic Collisions
topics.short: Combine conservation of momentum and of kinetic energy: the relative speed reverses in a one-dimensional elastic collision.

topics.title: Collisions in Two Dimensions
topics.short: Conserve the x- and y-components of momentum separately.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law for a System
topics.short: ΣF_external = M·a_cm, because the internal forces cancel in pairs.

topics.title: The Rocket Equation
topics.short: A rocket gains Δv = v_e ln(m₀/m_f) by throwing mass backward.

topics.title: Angular Velocity and Acceleration with Calculus
topics.short: ω = dθ/dt and α = dω/dt; integrate α(t) to find ω and θ.

topics.title: Moment of Inertia by Integration
topics.short: I = ∫r² dm gives the rotational inertia of rods, rings, disks and spheres.

topics.title: The Parallel-Axis Theorem
topics.short: I = I_cm + Md² for an axis shifted a distance d from the center of mass.

topics.title: Torque as a Cross Product
topics.short: τ = r × F, with its direction given by the right-hand rule.

topics.title: Rolling Dynamics
topics.short: Static friction makes rolling work: on a ramp a = g sin θ/(1 + I/(MR²)).

topics.title: From Skidding to Rolling
topics.short: A ball that starts out sliding skids until v = Rω, losing energy to kinetic friction on the way.

topics.title: Angular Momentum of a Particle
topics.short: L = r × p, so even a particle moving in a straight line has angular momentum about a point.

topics.title: Collisions with Rotation
topics.short: When a ball sticks to a pivoted rod, angular momentum about the pivot is conserved but linear momentum is not.

topics.title: Work and Power in Rotation
topics.short: W = ∫τ dθ and P = τω.

topics.title: Gyroscopes and Precession
topics.short: A torque at right angles to the spin turns the direction of L, so a top precesses at Ω = τ/L.

topics.title: Static Equilibrium Problems
topics.short: For ladders, hinged beams and hanging signs, choose a pivot that removes the unknowns you don't need.

topics.title: Gravity of a Spherical Body
topics.short: Outside a uniform sphere, gravity acts as if all the mass sat at the center; inside, g grows in proportion to r.

topics.title: Orbital Energy
topics.short: A circular orbit has E = −GMm/(2r), so climbing to a higher orbit takes energy yet leaves you moving more slowly.

topics.title: Kepler's Second Law from Angular Momentum
topics.short: Gravity exerts no torque about the Sun, so L is constant and equal areas are swept in equal times.

topics.title: Kepler's Third Law from Newton
topics.short: For a circular orbit T² = 4π²r³/(GM), which weighs a planet or star from its satellites.

topics.title: Speed on an Elliptical Orbit
topics.short: v² = GM(2/r − 1/a) gives the speed anywhere on an ellipse, which plans transfer orbits.

topics.title: The Equation of Simple Harmonic Motion
topics.short: x″ = −ω²x is solved by x = A cos(ωt + φ) with ω = √(k/m).

topics.title: Amplitude and Phase from Starting Conditions
topics.short: Use x(0) and v(0) to find the amplitude A and the phase φ.

topics.title: Springs Hanging Vertically
topics.short: Gravity only moves the equilibrium point; the period stays 2π√(m/k).

topics.title: Simple and Physical Pendulums
topics.short: A swinging rigid body has T = 2π√(I/(mgd)), and small angles make any pendulum simple harmonic.

topics.title: Damped Oscillations
topics.short: Drag makes the amplitude shrink as e^(−bt/2m), and too much damping stops the swinging altogether.

topics.title: Driven Oscillations and Resonance
topics.short: Pushing near the natural frequency builds a large amplitude, limited only by damping.

topics.title: The Wave Function y(x, t)
topics.short: A sinusoidal wave is y = A sin(kx − ωt), with k = 2π/λ, ω = 2πf and speed v = ω/k.

topics.title: The Wave Equation
topics.short: Any shape moving at speed v satisfies ∂²y/∂x² = (1/v²)·∂²y/∂t².

topics.title: Energy and Power of a Wave
topics.short: A wave on a string carries power P = ½μω²A²v, so doubling the amplitude carries four times the power.

topics.title: Phase Difference and Interference
topics.short: Two equal waves with phase difference φ add to amplitude 2A cos(φ/2), and a path difference Δr gives φ = 2πΔr/λ.

topics.title: Standing Waves as Two Traveling Waves
topics.short: Two opposite traveling waves add to y = 2A sin kx cos ωt, with nodes that never move.

topics.title: Sound as a Pressure Wave
topics.short: Sound is a pressure wave moving at v = √(B/ρ); pressure nodes sit where the displacement swings most.

topics.title: Beats
topics.short: Two tones of nearly equal frequency throb at the beat frequency |f₁ − f₂|.

topics.title: Shock Waves
topics.short: A source faster than sound drags a cone of wavefronts with sin θ = v_sound/v_source.

topics.title: Huygens' Principle
topics.short: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of wavelets, which explains refraction and diffraction.

topics.title: Polarization by Reflection
topics.short: Light reflected at Brewster's angle, tan θ_B = n₂/n₁, is completely polarized.

topics.title: Intensity in Interference Patterns
topics.short: Two slits give I = I₀cos²(πd sin θ/λ), and more slits make sharper bright lines.

topics.title: Single-Slit Envelopes and Missing Orders
topics.short: A single slit's pattern sets the envelope of a double-slit pattern, and some bright orders vanish.

topics.title: Resolution and the Rayleigh Criterion
topics.short: Two points can just be told apart when their angular separation is θ = 1.22λ/D.

topics.title: The Michelson Interferometer
topics.short: Moving one mirror a distance λ/2 shifts the pattern by one whole fringe.

topics.title: Antireflection Coatings and Air Wedges
topics.short: A quarter-wave coating cancels a reflection, and counting fringes in an air wedge measures tiny thicknesses.

topics.title: X-Ray Diffraction and Bragg's Law
topics.short: Crystal planes a distance d apart reflect X-rays strongly when 2d sin θ = mλ.

topics.title: The Lensmaker's Equation
topics.short: A lens's focal length comes from its shape and material: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂).

topics.title: Two-Lens Systems
topics.short: The image made by the first lens is the object for the second, and the magnifications multiply.

topics.title: The Eye and Corrective Lenses
topics.short: A lens's power is P = 1/f in diopters; nearsighted eyes need diverging lenses and farsighted eyes converging ones.

topics.title: Magnifiers and Microscopes
topics.short: A magnifier gives M = 25 cm/f, and a microscope multiplies the objective's magnification by the eyepiece's.

topics.title: Telescope Optics
topics.short: A refracting telescope magnifies by M = −f_objective/f_eyepiece, and its aperture sets how faint and how fine it can see.

topics.title: The Postulates of Relativity
topics.short: The laws of physics and the speed of light are the same in every inertial frame.

topics.title: The Relativity of Simultaneity
topics.short: Two events at the same time in one frame can happen at different times in another.

topics.title: Time Dilation
topics.short: A moving clock runs slow: Δt = γΔτ, with γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²).

topics.title: Length Contraction
topics.short: A moving object is shorter along its motion: L = L₀/γ.

topics.title: The Lorentz Transformation
topics.short: x′ = γ(x − vt) and t′ = γ(t − vx/c²) convert events between frames.

topics.title: Spacetime Diagrams and the Interval
topics.short: The interval s² = (cΔt)² − Δx² is the same for every observer.

topics.title: Relativistic Velocity Addition
topics.short: Velocities combine as u′ = (u − v)/(1 − uv/c²), so no speed passes c.

topics.title: The Relativistic Doppler Effect
topics.short: Light from an approaching source arrives at f = f₀√((1 + β)/(1 − β)), with β = v/c.

topics.title: Relativistic Momentum and Energy
topics.short: p = γmu and E = γmc², linked by E² = (pc)² + (mc²)².

topics.title: Planck and Blackbody Radiation
topics.short: Planck's quantized energies explain the blackbody spectrum, and Wien's and Stefan's laws follow from it.

topics.title: The Compton Formula
topics.short: Conserving energy and momentum gives Δλ = (h/mc)(1 − cos θ).

topics.title: The Bohr Model of Hydrogen
topics.short: Quantized angular momentum gives E_n = −13.6 eV/n² and r_n = n²a₀.

topics.title: Hydrogen's Spectral Series
topics.short: Lyman, Balmer and Paschen lines follow 1/λ = R(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²).

topics.title: The Uncertainty Principle
topics.short: Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2: the more sharply a position is fixed, the more spread its momentum must have.

topics.title: Wave Functions and Probability
topics.short: |ψ|² is a probability density, normalized so the total probability is 1.

topics.title: The Schrödinger Equation
topics.short: −(ħ²/2m)ψ″ + Uψ = Eψ: check whether a function solves it and read off its energy.

topics.title: A Particle in a Box
topics.short: Confining a particle to a length L allows only E_n = n²h²/(8mL²).

topics.title: Finite Wells and Tunneling
topics.short: Wave functions leak into barriers, so a particle can tunnel through one with probability about e^(−2κL).

topics.title: The Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
topics.short: The energies are evenly spaced, E_n = (n + ½)ħω, starting from a nonzero zero-point energy.

topics.title: Quantum Numbers in Hydrogen
topics.short: The labels n, l, m_l and m_s name each state, and shell n holds 2n² states.

topics.title: Electron Spin and the Exclusion Principle
topics.short: No two electrons in an atom share all four quantum numbers, which builds the periodic table.

topics.title: Conductors, Insulators and Semiconductors
topics.short: Energy bands and the gaps between them decide how a solid conducts, and doping and LEDs follow from them.

topics.title: Nuclear Size and Binding Energy per Nucleon
topics.short: Nuclei have radius R = r₀A^(1/3), and the binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron.

topics.title: The Exponential Decay Law
topics.short: N = N₀e^(−λt), the activity is A = λN, and the half-life is ln 2/λ.

topics.title: Energy in Nuclear Reactions
topics.short: Q = (mass before − mass after)c², at 931.5 MeV for each atomic mass unit.

topics.title: Radioactive Dating
topics.short: The fraction of a parent isotope left gives an age: t = (T½/ln 2)·ln(N₀/N).

topics.title: Leptons, Hadrons and Quarks
topics.short: Leptons are fundamental, baryons hold three quarks and mesons a quark and an antiquark.

topics.title: Antiparticles, Pair Production and Annihilation
topics.short: Making an electron–positron pair takes at least 2mc², and annihilation turns the pair back into gamma rays.

topics.title: Conservation Laws in Particle Reactions
topics.short: Charge, baryon number and lepton number decide which reactions can happen.

topics.title: The Four Forces and Their Carriers
topics.short: Gravity, electromagnetism and the weak and strong forces; the last three are carried by photons, W and Z bosons and gluons.

topics.title: Checking Equations with Units
topics.short: Every term in a physics equation must have the same units, which catches many mistakes before they happen.

topics.title: Position and Displacement on an Axis
topics.short: Pick an origin and a positive direction; displacement Δx = x_final − x_initial carries a sign.

topics.title: Average Velocity
topics.short: Average velocity is Δx/Δt, with a sign; average speed uses total distance instead.

topics.title: Position-Time Graphs
topics.short: The slope of an x–t graph is the velocity.

topics.title: Instantaneous Velocity
topics.short: The velocity at an instant is the slope of the tangent line to the x–t graph.

topics.title: Acceleration and Its Sign
topics.short: a = Δv/Δt; an object slows down when its acceleration points opposite to its velocity.

topics.title: Velocity-Time Graphs
topics.short: On a v–t graph the slope is the acceleration and the area under the line is the displacement.

topics.title: Translating Between Motion Graphs
topics.short: Turn an x–t graph into v–t and a–t graphs, and back again.

topics.title: The Constant-Acceleration Equations
topics.short: v = v₀ + at and x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at² hold when the acceleration is constant.

topics.title: Motion Without the Time
topics.short: v² = v₀² + 2aΔx links speeds and displacement when the time isn't known.

topics.title: Free Fall
topics.short: Without air resistance, every dropped object speeds up by 9.8 m/s each second, whatever its mass.

topics.title: Thrown Straight Up
topics.short: Going up, at the top and coming down, the acceleration is the same 9.8 m/s² downward.

topics.title: Vectors and Their Components
topics.short: Split a vector into x- and y-components with sine and cosine.

topics.title: Adding Vectors by Components
topics.short: Add the x-parts and the y-parts, then find the size and direction of the result.

topics.title: Relative Velocity
topics.short: Velocities add as vectors when you change reference frames: boats in rivers, planes in wind.

topics.title: Launched Horizontally
topics.short: Horizontal motion stays steady while vertical motion is free fall, and both share the same time.

topics.title: Launched at an Angle
topics.short: Split the launch velocity into parts, treat each direction on its own, and use the symmetry of the path.

topics.title: Systems and Center of Mass
topics.short: Choose what is in your system; its center of mass is the mass-weighted average position.

topics.title: Free-Body Diagrams
topics.short: Draw every force on one object as an arrow from its center, naming what exerts it.

topics.title: Newton's Third Law Pairs
topics.short: The two forces of a pair act on different objects, are the same type and are equal in size.

topics.title: Equilibrium and the First Law
topics.short: Zero net force means constant velocity, and standing still is the special case where that velocity is zero.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law Along an Axis
topics.short: Add the forces along an axis with signs, then a = ΣF/m.

topics.title: The Normal Force and Apparent Weight
topics.short: A surface pushes as hard as it must; in an accelerating elevator the scale reading differs from mg.

topics.title: Forces at Angles
topics.short: Resolve each force into components; the x and y directions each obey Newton's second law separately.

topics.title: Inclined Planes
topics.short: On a ramp at angle θ, gravity splits into mg sin θ along the slope and mg cos θ into it.

topics.title: Kinetic Friction
topics.short: A sliding object feels friction f_k = μ_k N against its sliding.

topics.title: Static Friction
topics.short: Static friction matches the push up to a limit of μ_s N; beyond that, the object slides.

topics.title: Friction on Ramps
topics.short: Find the angle where a block starts to slip, tan θ = μ_s, and its acceleration once it slides.

topics.title: Connected Objects and Tension
topics.short: Treat linked objects as one system to find a, then one object alone to find the tension.

topics.title: Pulleys and the Atwood Machine
topics.short: A light rope over a light pulley has one tension, and the whole system speeds up together.

topics.title: Spring Forces and Hooke's Law
topics.short: A stretched or squeezed spring pushes back with F = kx, in proportion to how far it is stretched or squeezed.

topics.title: Newton's Law of Gravitation
topics.short: F = Gm₁m₂/r², with r measured between the centers.

topics.title: Gravitational Field Strength
topics.short: g = GM/r² is the gravitational force on each kilogram near a planet.

topics.title: Centripetal Acceleration
topics.short: Moving in a circle at steady speed means accelerating toward the center: a = v²/r.

topics.title: Forces in Circular Motion
topics.short: A real force such as tension, friction or gravity supplies the net inward force mv²/r.

topics.title: Vertical Circles
topics.short: At the top and bottom of a loop or a dip, the net force toward the center is mv²/r.

topics.title: Work by a Constant Force
topics.short: W = Fd cos θ, and a force at right angles to the motion does no work.

topics.title: Work as Area Under a Force Graph
topics.short: The area under a force–position graph is the work done.

topics.title: The Work-Energy Theorem
topics.short: The net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

topics.title: Gravitational Potential Energy of a System
topics.short: ΔU = mgΔh belongs to the Earth–object system, and only changes in it matter.

topics.title: Elastic Potential Energy
topics.short: A spring stretched or squeezed by x stores ½kx².

topics.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
topics.short: When only gravity and springs do work, K + U stays the same.

topics.title: Energy Bar Charts
topics.short: Show the energy at the start, the energy that crosses the system boundary, and the energy at the end.

topics.title: Friction and Thermal Energy
topics.short: Friction turns mechanical energy into thermal energy: ΔE_thermal = f_k d.

topics.title: Power
topics.short: Power is the rate of energy transfer: P = W/Δt = Fv.

topics.title: Gravitational Potential Energy Far from Earth
topics.short: U = −Gm₁m₂/r, which is zero when the objects are infinitely far apart.

topics.title: Linear Momentum
topics.short: Momentum p = mv is a vector, and a system's momentum is the vector sum of its parts.

topics.title: Impulse and Change in Momentum
topics.short: FΔt = Δp, and the area under a force–time graph is the impulse.

topics.title: Conservation of Momentum
topics.short: With no net outside force, the total momentum of a system stays the same.

topics.title: Sticking Collisions
topics.short: Objects that stick move off together: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v.

topics.title: Elastic and Inelastic Collisions
topics.short: Kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions; compare K before and after to classify one.

topics.title: Explosions and Recoil
topics.short: Pieces that start at rest fly apart with equal and opposite momenta.

topics.title: Motion of the Center of Mass
topics.short: With no outside force, a system's center of mass keeps moving at a steady velocity.

topics.title: Angle, Angular Velocity and Angular Acceleration
topics.short: Measure turning in radians: ω = Δθ/Δt and α = Δω/Δt.

topics.title: Rotational Kinematics
topics.short: ω = ω₀ + αt and θ = ω₀t + ½αt² mirror the straight-line equations.

topics.title: Linking Linear and Rotational Motion
topics.short: A point at radius r moves with v = rω and tangential acceleration a = rα.

topics.title: Torque
topics.short: Torque is a force times its lever arm: τ = rF sin θ.

topics.title: Rotational Equilibrium
topics.short: A balanced object has zero net force and zero net torque about any point you choose.

topics.title: Rotational Inertia
topics.short: I = Σmr²: mass far from the axis makes an object harder to spin.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law for Rotation
topics.short: The net torque equals Iα.

topics.title: Pulleys with Mass
topics.short: Solve a hanging mass on a heavy pulley with τ = Iα and F = ma together.

topics.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Work by Torque
topics.short: A spinning object stores ½Iω², and a torque turning it through Δθ does work τΔθ.

topics.title: Rolling Without Slipping
topics.short: A rolling object shares its energy between moving and spinning, so a hoop rolls down a ramp more slowly than a ball.

topics.title: Angular Momentum and Angular Impulse
topics.short: L = Iω for a spinning object and L = mvr⊥ for a passing point mass; a torque acting for a time changes L by τΔt.

topics.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum
topics.short: With no outside torque Iω stays the same, so a skater who pulls in her arms spins faster.

topics.title: Satellites in Orbit
topics.short: Gravity supplies the centripetal force, so v = √(GM/r) and lower orbits are faster.

topics.title: Simple Harmonic Motion
topics.short: A restoring force proportional to displacement makes motion repeat with a fixed amplitude, period and frequency.

topics.title: Period of a Mass on a Spring
topics.short: T = 2π√(m/k), whatever the amplitude.

topics.title: Period of a Pendulum
topics.short: For small swings T = 2π√(L/g), and the mass of the bob doesn't matter.

topics.title: Energy in Simple Harmonic Motion
topics.short: Energy swaps between ½kx² and ½mv², and the total is ½kA².

topics.title: Graphs of Simple Harmonic Motion
topics.short: Position, velocity and acceleration follow sine and cosine curves, each a quarter cycle apart.

topics.title: Pressure and Depth
topics.short: In a still fluid P = P₀ + ρgh, and gauge pressure leaves out the air pressure above.

topics.title: Pascal's Principle and Hydraulics
topics.short: A pressure change spreads through a confined fluid, so a small force on a small piston lifts a heavy load.

topics.title: Buoyant Force and Archimedes' Principle
topics.short: The fluid pushes up with the weight of the fluid displaced, F_b = ρ_fluid·V·g, and a floating object displaces its own weight.

topics.title: Flow Rate and Continuity
topics.short: For a liquid filling a pipe, the flow rate Av is the same everywhere: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂.

topics.title: Bernoulli's Equation
topics.short: Along a streamline P + ½ρv² + ρgh stays the same, so faster-moving fluid has lower pressure.

topics.title: The Ideal Gas Law
topics.short: PV = nRT = Nk_BT, with the temperature in kelvins.

topics.title: Temperature and Molecular Energy
topics.short: Each gas molecule has average kinetic energy (3/2)k_BT, so a monatomic gas holds internal energy U = (3/2)nRT.

topics.title: Latent Heat
topics.short: Melting or boiling a mass m takes Q = mL; add the warming stages to find the total heat.

topics.title: Rate of Heat Conduction
topics.short: Heat flows through a slab at the rate P = kAΔT/L, so thinner and wider walls pass more.

topics.title: Thermal Radiation and Blackbodies
topics.short: Every object radiates P = eσAT⁴, and hotter objects glow at shorter peak wavelengths: λ_max·T = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K.

topics.title: Work Done on a Gas
topics.short: W = −PΔV is the work done on the gas, and its size is the area under the path on a P–V diagram.

topics.title: The First Law of Thermodynamics
topics.short: ΔU = Q + W: the internal energy changes by the heat added plus the work done on the gas.

topics.title: Isobaric, Isochoric, Isothermal and Adiabatic Processes
topics.short: Each process holds one thing fixed, which decides how Q, W and ΔU split.

topics.title: Cycles on a P–V Diagram
topics.short: Around a closed cycle ΔU = 0, and the area enclosed is the net work.

topics.title: Heat Engines and Efficiency
topics.short: An engine turns part of the heat Q_H into work and gives off the rest as Q_C, with efficiency e = W/Q_H.

topics.title: The Carnot Limit
topics.short: No engine running between T_H and T_C can beat e = 1 − T_C/T_H, with temperatures in kelvins.

topics.title: Refrigerators and Heat Pumps
topics.short: Work can move heat from cold to hot, and a heat pump delivers more heat than the work it uses.

topics.title: Entropy and the Second Law
topics.short: Heat flows from hot to cold on its own; ΔS = Q/T, and the total entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

topics.title: Charge, Conductors and Charging
topics.short: Charge comes in whole multiples of e and is conserved, and objects charge by friction, contact or induction.

topics.title: Coulomb's Law
topics.short: F = k|q₁q₂|/r²: double the distance and the force drops to a quarter.

topics.title: Adding Electric Forces
topics.short: The net force on a charge is the vector sum of the forces from each of the other charges.

topics.title: The Electric Field
topics.short: E = F/q is the force on each coulomb; a point charge makes E = k|q|/r², pointing away from a positive charge.

topics.title: Fields of Several Charges and Field Lines
topics.short: Add the field vectors from each charge; field lines show the direction, and their spacing shows the strength.

topics.title: Charges in a Uniform Field
topics.short: Between parallel plates E is uniform, so a charge feels a constant force qE and moves like a projectile.

topics.title: Electric Potential Energy
topics.short: Two charges store U = kq₁q₂/r, positive when they repel and negative when they attract.

topics.title: Electric Potential and Voltage
topics.short: Potential is energy per charge, V = kq/r near a point charge, and a charge crossing ΔV gains or loses qΔV of kinetic energy.

topics.title: Equipotentials and Field Strength
topics.short: The field points from high to low potential, at right angles to equipotentials, with E = ΔV/d between plates.

topics.title: Capacitors
topics.short: C = Q/V, and for parallel plates C = κε₀A/d.

topics.title: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
topics.short: A charged capacitor stores U = ½QV = ½CV².

topics.title: Electric Current
topics.short: I = ΔQ/Δt, and conventional current points the way positive charge would flow.

topics.title: Resistance and Resistivity
topics.short: R = ρL/A, so longer and thinner wires resist more.

topics.title: Power in Resistors
topics.short: P = IV = I²R = V²/R are three forms of one idea.

topics.title: Resistors in Series
topics.short: One current passes through every resistor, the voltages add, and R_eq = R₁ + R₂ + ⋯.

topics.title: Resistors in Parallel
topics.short: Each branch has the same voltage, 1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ⋯, and adding a branch lowers R_eq.

topics.title: Series-Parallel Combinations
topics.short: Reduce a circuit step by step, then work back out to find each current and voltage.

topics.title: Kirchhoff's Junction Rule
topics.short: The current flowing into a junction equals the current flowing out, because charge is conserved.

topics.title: Kirchhoff's Loop Rule
topics.short: The voltage changes around any closed loop add to zero, because energy is conserved.

topics.title: EMF and Internal Resistance
topics.short: A real battery's terminal voltage is ε − Ir, so it sags as the current grows.

topics.title: Capacitors in Series and Parallel
topics.short: Parallel capacitances add, and series capacitances combine by reciprocals, the opposite of resistors.

topics.title: RC Circuits
topics.short: A capacitor charges through a resistor with time constant τ = RC, and once full it blocks steady current.

topics.title: Magnetic Fields and Their Sources
topics.short: Magnets and moving charges make magnetic fields, measured in teslas, whose lines form closed loops.

topics.title: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
topics.short: F = qvB sin θ, at right angles to both v and B, by the right-hand rule.

topics.title: Charges Circling in a Magnetic Field
topics.short: The magnetic force is centripetal, so r = mv/(|q|B), and it never changes the speed.

topics.title: Magnetic Force on a Current
topics.short: A wire carrying current I across a field B feels F = ILB sin θ.

topics.title: Fields of Wires and Solenoids
topics.short: A long wire makes B = μ₀I/(2πr) in circles around it, a solenoid makes a nearly uniform B = μ₀nI inside, and parallel currents attract.

topics.title: Magnetic Flux
topics.short: Φ = BA cos θ counts the field passing through a loop, with θ measured from the loop's normal.

topics.title: Faraday's Law
topics.short: A changing magnetic flux makes an emf: ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt.

topics.title: Lenz's Law
topics.short: The induced current makes a field that opposes the change in flux.

topics.title: Motional EMF
topics.short: A rod sliding along rails at speed v makes ε = BLv, and the force on the induced current slows the rod.

topics.title: Reflection and Plane Mirrors
topics.short: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, and a plane mirror's image is as far behind it as the object is in front.

topics.title: Index of Refraction
topics.short: n = c/v: light slows in glass and water, and its wavelength shrinks while its frequency stays the same.

topics.title: Snell's Law
topics.short: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, with angles measured from the normal.

topics.title: Total Internal Reflection
topics.short: Going from higher to lower n, light beyond the critical angle, sin θc = n₂/n₁, reflects completely.

topics.title: Curved Mirrors and Ray Diagrams
topics.short: Three principal rays locate the image formed by a concave or convex mirror.

topics.title: The Mirror Equation
topics.short: 1/f = 1/dₒ + 1/dᵢ and m = −dᵢ/dₒ, with signs that mark real and virtual images.

topics.title: Lenses and Ray Diagrams
topics.short: Converging and diverging lenses bend parallel rays toward or away from a focal point.

topics.title: The Thin Lens Equation
topics.short: The mirror equation works for lenses too, and real images form on the far side of the lens.

topics.title: What Sets a Wave's Speed
topics.short: The medium sets the speed, v = √(tension/μ) on a string, and the source sets the frequency.

topics.title: Snapshot and History Graphs
topics.short: A y–x graph shows the whole wave at one instant; a y–t graph follows one point over time.

topics.title: Reflection at Boundaries
topics.short: A pulse reflects upside down from a fixed end and right side up from a free end, and partly passes into a new medium.

topics.title: Electromagnetic Waves
topics.short: Light is a wave of linked electric and magnetic fields moving through empty space at c = fλ.

topics.title: Polarization
topics.short: Only transverse waves can be polarized; a polarizer passes half of unpolarized light and I₀cos²θ of polarized light.

topics.title: Superposition and Interference
topics.short: Overlapping waves add point by point: crest on crest builds up, crest on trough cancels.

topics.title: Standing Waves on Strings
topics.short: A string fixed at both ends resonates at fₙ = nv/(2L).

topics.title: Standing Sound Waves in Pipes
topics.short: Open pipes resonate at fₙ = nv/(2L); pipes closed at one end only at odd multiples of v/(4L).

topics.title: Sound Intensity and Decibels
topics.short: Intensity falls off as 1/r², and β = 10 log(I/I₀), so adding 10 dB means 10 times the intensity.

topics.title: The Doppler Effect
topics.short: A source moving toward you sounds higher and one moving away sounds lower: f′ = f·v/(v ∓ vₛ).

topics.title: Diffraction
topics.short: Waves spread out past an opening, and a single slit makes dark fringes where a sin θ = mλ.

topics.title: Double-Slit Interference
topics.short: Bright fringes appear where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths: d sin θ = mλ.

topics.title: Diffraction Gratings
topics.short: Many evenly spaced slits make sharp bright lines at d sin θ = mλ, where d is 1 divided by the number of lines per meter.

topics.title: Thin-Film Interference
topics.short: Light reflecting from the top and bottom of a thin film interferes, with a half-wave flip at each reflection off a higher index.

topics.title: Photons
topics.short: Light comes in photons of energy E = hf = hc/λ, and 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

topics.title: The Photoelectric Effect
topics.short: An electron escapes a metal only if a single photon brings more than the work function: Kₘₐₓ = hf − φ.

topics.title: The Bohr Model and Energy Levels
topics.short: Electrons in atoms have only certain energies, and a jump between levels absorbs or emits a photon whose energy is the difference between the two levels.

topics.title: Emission and Absorption Spectra
topics.short: A hot thin gas emits bright lines, and the same gas in front of a hotter source absorbs those same lines.

topics.title: Matter Waves
topics.short: Particles have a wavelength λ = h/p, so electrons diffract like light.

topics.title: Compton Scattering
topics.short: A photon carries momentum p = h/λ, so an X-ray that bounces off an electron comes away with a longer wavelength.

topics.title: Mass-Energy and Binding Energy
topics.short: E = mc²: a nucleus has less mass than its separate protons and neutrons, and the missing mass is its binding energy.

topics.title: Average Speed
topics.short: Average speed is total distance divided by total time: s = d/t.

topics.title: Distance-Time Graphs
topics.short: A steeper line means faster; a flat line means stopped.

topics.title: Distance and Displacement
topics.short: Distance is how far you traveled; displacement is how far and which way you ended up from the start.

topics.title: Velocity: Speed with a Direction
topics.short: Velocity tells how fast and which way, so turning around changes it even at the same speed.

topics.title: Acceleration
topics.short: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes: a = Δv/Δt, in meters per second per second.

topics.title: Speed-Time Graphs
topics.short: On a speed-time graph a rising line means speeding up and a flat line means steady speed.

topics.title: What a Force Is
topics.short: A force is a push or pull between two objects, measured in newtons.

topics.title: Net Force and Balanced Forces
topics.short: Add forces along a line, counting direction, to find the net force.

topics.title: Newton's First Law: Inertia
topics.short: With zero net force, an object keeps the velocity it has, whether still or moving.

topics.title: Newton's Second Law: F = ma
topics.short: Net force equals mass times acceleration, so the same push speeds up a heavy cart less.

topics.title: Mass and Weight
topics.short: Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the pull of gravity on it: W = mg, with g = 9.8 N/kg on Earth.

topics.title: Friction
topics.short: Friction acts where surfaces touch, against their sliding, and grows when they press together harder.

topics.title: Newton's Third Law
topics.short: Forces come in pairs: when A pushes B, B pushes A just as hard in the opposite direction.

topics.title: Momentum
topics.short: Momentum is mass times velocity, and in a collision the total momentum stays the same.

topics.title: Softening a Collision
topics.short: Stretching a collision over more time lowers the force, which is how airbags, helmets and crumple zones work.

topics.title: Gravity: Mass and Distance
topics.short: Every two masses attract; more mass means more pull, and twice the distance means a quarter of the pull.

topics.title: Pressure
topics.short: Pressure is force spread over an area: P = F/A, in pascals (newtons per square meter).

topics.title: Forms of Energy
topics.short: Energy shows up as motion, height, stretch, heat, light, sound, chemical and electric energy.

topics.title: Kinetic Energy
topics.short: KE = ½mv², so doubling the speed gives four times the energy.

topics.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
topics.short: Lifting an object stores energy: PE = mgh, measured from a chosen level.

topics.title: Energy Changes Form
topics.short: As an object falls or swings, energy moves between kinetic and potential, and the total stays the same.

topics.title: Work
topics.short: Work is force times the distance moved along the force: W = Fd, in joules.

topics.title: Power
topics.short: Power is how fast energy is transferred: P = W/t, in watts.

topics.title: Efficiency
topics.short: Efficiency is useful energy out divided by energy in, and it is always less than 100%.

topics.title: Simple Machines and Mechanical Advantage
topics.short: Ramps, levers and pulleys trade a smaller force for a longer distance.

topics.title: Levers and Balance
topics.short: A lever balances when force times distance from the pivot is the same on both sides.

topics.title: Conduction, Convection and Radiation
topics.short: Heat moves by contact, by moving fluids and by light, including infrared you can't see.

topics.title: Changes of State
topics.short: Melting and boiling take in energy without raising the temperature; freezing and condensing give it back.

topics.title: Parts of a Wave
topics.short: Amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period describe a wave; the period is 1 divided by the frequency.

topics.title: The Wave Equation v = fλ
topics.short: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.

topics.title: Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
topics.short: In a transverse wave the medium moves across the wave's path; in a longitudinal wave it moves back and forth along it.

topics.title: Sound: Pitch and Loudness
topics.short: Pitch comes from frequency and loudness from amplitude, and sound needs a medium to travel.

topics.title: Echoes and Sonar
topics.short: Time an echo to find a distance: d = vt/2, because the sound goes there and back.

topics.title: Reflection, Absorption and Transmission
topics.short: When a wave meets a new material it can bounce off, be absorbed or pass through.

topics.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
topics.short: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are all light, with different wavelengths.

topics.title: Light and Color
topics.short: White light holds all colors, and objects look colored by the light they reflect.

topics.title: Refraction and Lenses
topics.short: Light bends when it changes speed at a boundary at an angle, and lenses use this to focus.

topics.title: Higher Frequency, More Energy
topics.short: Light comes in tiny packets whose energy rises with frequency, so one ultraviolet or X-ray packet can break molecules in cells and one radio packet can't.

topics.title: Analog and Digital Signals
topics.short: A digital signal sends information as separate values (0s and 1s), which can still be read exactly after some noise is added.

topics.title: Electric Charge
topics.short: Protons are positive and electrons negative; objects become charged by gaining or losing electrons, while the protons stay put.

topics.title: Attraction and Repulsion
topics.short: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract, more strongly when they are closer.

topics.title: Fields: Forces at a Distance
topics.short: Gravity, electric and magnetic forces act across space through fields around objects.

topics.title: Current and Voltage
topics.short: Current is the flow of charge, in amperes; voltage is the push given to each charge, in volts.

topics.title: Complete Circuits
topics.short: Charge flows only around a closed loop, and a switch opens or closes the loop.

topics.title: Ohm's Law
topics.short: Voltage equals current times resistance: V = IR.

topics.title: Series and Parallel Circuits
topics.short: In series one current flows through everything; in parallel each branch gets the full voltage.

topics.title: Electric Power and Energy Use
topics.short: P = VI, and the energy used is power times time, often in kilowatt-hours.

topics.title: Magnets and Magnetic Fields
topics.short: Every magnet has a north and a south pole, and its field lines run from north to south outside it.

topics.title: Electromagnets and Motors
topics.short: An electric current makes a magnetic field; a coil around iron makes it much stronger.

topics.title: Generators and Induction
topics.short: Moving a magnet near a coil makes a current, so generators turn motion into electricity.

topics.title: Units and Significant Figures
topics.short: Change feet to meters and miles to feet with conversion factors, and keep only as many digits as the measurement deserves.

topics.title: Graphing Flight Data
topics.short: Read a rocket's velocity-time graph: the slope is acceleration, the area is height, and the top of the flight is where the line crosses zero.

topics.title: Statistics of Repeated Launches
topics.short: Fly the same rocket again and again: the mean says what to expect, and the range and standard deviation say how much to trust it.

topics.title: Newton's Three Laws and Thrust
topics.short: A rocket pushes its exhaust down and the exhaust pushes the rocket up. Net force, not thrust alone, sets the acceleration.

topics.title: Thrust-to-Weight and Liftoff
topics.short: A rocket leaves the pad only if its thrust beats its weight. The ratio of the two tells how hard it jumps and how fast it leaves the launch rod.

topics.title: Impulse, Momentum and Thrust Curves
topics.short: Total impulse is the area under the thrust curve. It equals the change in momentum, and it is what a motor's letter class measures.

topics.title: Mass Flow and the Rocket Equation
topics.short: As a rocket throws mass backward it gets lighter. Adding up those small pushes with calculus gives Tsiolkovsky's equation, $\Delta v = v_e \ln(m_0/m_f)$.

topics.title: Nozzles in Concept
topics.short: Why a rocket nozzle narrows and then widens: pressure turns into exhaust speed, and faster exhaust means more thrust from the same mass flow.

topics.title: Calculus of Motion
topics.short: Velocity is the derivative of height, and the change in velocity is the area under the acceleration graph.

topics.title: Powered Flight to Burnout
topics.short: While the motor burns, the net force gives a steady acceleration (in a simple model). Burnout speed and height follow from the kinematic equations.

topics.title: Free Fall and Coasting to Apogee
topics.short: After burnout the rocket is still going up, slowing by 9.8 m/s every second until it stops at apogee.

topics.title: Energy From Burnout to Apogee
topics.short: Kinetic energy at burnout turns into potential energy on the way up. Comparing the two shows how much energy drag took.

topics.title: Drag: A First Look, Then a Numerical Step
topics.short: Air pushes back harder the faster you go, about as the square of speed. With drag there is no neat formula, so we step through the flight a little at a time.

topics.title: Stability: Center of Mass and Center of Pressure
topics.short: A rocket flies straight when its center of mass is ahead of its center of pressure, so a gust turns it back into the wind like a weather vane.

topics.title: Projectile Range and Launch Angle
topics.short: Tilt the flight and some of the speed carries the rocket sideways. Range depends on the angle, with the longest at 45 degrees in the ideal case.

topics.title: Altitude by the Tangent
topics.short: Stand a measured distance from the pad, sight the rocket at its highest point, and the tangent of the angle times the baseline gives its height.

topics.title: How Good Is the Estimate?
topics.short: A one-degree slip in the angle changes the height by an amount that grows fast at steep angles. Choosing the baseline well keeps the error small.

topics.title: Triangulating From Two Observers
topics.short: Two people sighting the same rocket from two places can find its height without measuring the distance to the rocket at all.

topics.title: Why Sputnik Didn't Fall
topics.short: An orbiting satellite is falling all the time, but it moves sideways so fast that the ground curves away beneath it.

topics.title: Escape Velocity
topics.short: Fast enough and an object never comes back: kinetic energy beats the whole gravitational well. Escape speed is $\sqrt{2}$ times circular orbit speed.

topics.title: Ellipses and Kepler's Laws
topics.short: Real orbits are ellipses with Earth at one focus. The satellite speeds up near the low point, and the size of the ellipse sets the period.

topics.title: Observing and Asking Questions
topics.short: Scientists look closely, use their senses and tools, and ask questions they can test. An observation is what you notice; a guess about why is a hypothesis.

topics.title: A Fair Test
topics.short: In a fair test you change only one thing, keep everything else the same, and measure what happens. Then you can tell what made the difference.

topics.title: Measuring Like a Scientist
topics.short: Length in centimeters and meters, mass in grams and kilograms, liquid volume in milliliters and liters, and temperature in degrees. Read the scale at eye level.

topics.title: What Is Matter?
topics.short: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Air is matter too: a balloon gets bigger when you fill it, and a full ball weighs a little more than a flat one.

topics.title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
topics.short: A solid keeps its own shape. A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps its amount. A gas spreads out to fill any container.

topics.title: Melting, Freezing and Boiling
topics.short: Heating can melt a solid into a liquid and turn a liquid into a gas. Cooling does the reverse. Water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) and boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at sea level.

topics.title: Mixtures and Solutions
topics.short: A mixture is two or more things mixed together that keep their own properties. In a solution, one thing dissolves evenly into another, like salt in water. The total mass stays the same.

topics.title: Changes That Make Something New
topics.short: A physical change (cutting, melting, dissolving) keeps the same substance. A chemical change makes a new substance: signs are a gas, a new color, light, heat or a smell.

topics.title: Pushes and Pulls
topics.short: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start something moving, stop it, speed it up, slow it down or change its direction. Balanced forces cancel; unbalanced forces change motion.

topics.title: Friction and Gravity
topics.short: Friction is a force that rubs against motion; rough surfaces make more of it. Gravity pulls things toward the center of the Earth, so dropped things fall down.

topics.title: Levers
topics.short: A lever is a stiff bar that turns on a point called the fulcrum. Pushing far from the fulcrum lets a small push lift a big load.

topics.title: Wheels, Axles and Pulleys
topics.short: A wheel and axle turn together: a small turn of the axle makes a big turn of the wheel, or the other way. A pulley is a wheel with a rope; a movable pulley halves the pull you need.

topics.title: Ramps, Wedges and Screws
topics.short: A ramp (inclined plane) lets you raise a load with a smaller push over a longer path. A wedge is two ramps back to back that split things apart. A screw is a ramp wrapped around a post.

topics.title: Forms of Energy
topics.short: Energy is what makes things move, light up, heat up or make sound. Its forms include motion, stored (in food, batteries, a stretched rubber band or something high up), heat, light, sound and electrical energy.

topics.title: Energy Changes Form
topics.short: Energy is never used up; it changes from one form to another. A flashlight turns stored energy in the battery into electrical energy, then light and some heat.

topics.title: How Heat Moves
topics.short: Heat moves from warmer things to cooler things. It moves by touching (conduction), by moving air or water (convection) and by rays like sunshine (radiation). Insulators slow it down.

topics.title: Magnets
topics.short: A magnet has a north pole and a south pole. Opposite poles attract and like poles repel. Magnets pull on iron and steel, but not on wood, plastic, paper, glass or most coins.

topics.title: Circuits
topics.short: Electricity flows only around a complete loop called a closed circuit: from the battery, through the wires and the bulb, and back. A switch opens the loop to turn the bulb off.

topics.title: Conductors and Insulators
topics.short: Conductors, like metals, let electricity flow through them. Insulators, like plastic, rubber, wood and glass, do not. Wires are metal inside and plastic outside.

topics.title: Electromagnets and Motors
topics.short: Electricity flowing through a coil of wire makes a magnet that can be turned on and off. Electromagnets lift scrap metal and turn the motors in fans and toys.

topics.title: Light and Shadows
topics.short: Light travels in straight lines. When something blocks it, a shadow forms on the other side. The closer the object is to the light, the bigger its shadow.

topics.title: Mirrors and Bending Light
topics.short: Light bounces off a mirror at the same angle it hits it. Light bends when it passes from air into water or glass, so a straw in a glass looks broken.

topics.title: White Light and Colors
topics.short: White light is a mix of all the colors of the rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. A prism or raindrops spread them out. A red apple looks red because it reflects red light.

topics.title: Sound and Vibrations
topics.short: Sound is made when something vibrates. Fast vibrations make a high pitch; slow ones a low pitch. Bigger vibrations are louder. Sound travels through air, water and solids, but not through empty space.

topics.title: The Water Cycle
topics.short: The Sun warms water so it evaporates into vapor. The vapor rises, cools and condenses into clouds. Water falls as rain or snow (precipitation) and collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and the ground.

topics.title: Weather and Its Tools
topics.short: Weather is the air outside today: temperature, wind, clouds and rain. A thermometer measures temperature, a rain gauge rain, a wind vane wind direction and an anemometer wind speed.

topics.title: Rocks and Minerals
topics.short: Rocks are made of minerals. Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools, sedimentary rock from layers of sand and mud pressed together, and metamorphic rock when heat and pressure change a rock.

topics.title: Weathering and Erosion
topics.short: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces; water, ice, wind and plant roots all do it. Erosion carries the pieces away, and they are dropped somewhere else, building new land.

topics.title: How Plants Make Food
topics.short: Plants make their own food (a sugar) in their leaves from sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the air. They give off oxygen. Roots take in water; they do not "eat" soil.

topics.title: Food Chains and Food Webs
topics.short: Energy starts with the Sun. Producers (plants) make food; consumers eat plants or other animals; decomposers break down dead things. A food web is many food chains joined together.

topics.title: Adaptations
topics.short: An adaptation is a body part or behavior that helps a living thing survive where it lives: a camel's hump of fat, a duck's webbed feet, a cactus's spines and waxy skin, birds flying south.

topics.title: The Human Body
topics.short: Body systems work together. Bones hold you up and muscles move them. The heart pumps blood; the lungs bring in oxygen; the stomach and intestines break down food; the brain and nerves send messages.

topics.title: Day, Night and the Sun's Path
topics.short: The Earth spins once about every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day; the other side has night. The Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west because the Earth turns.

topics.title: Phases of the Moon
topics.short: The Moon makes no light of its own; it reflects sunlight. As it goes around the Earth, about once a month, we see more or less of its sunlit half: new, crescent, quarter, gibbous and full.

topics.title: The Sun and Its Planets
topics.short: The Sun is a star, the closest one to us. Eight planets go around it: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Gravity keeps them in their orbits.

topics.title: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
topics.short: Pure substances have a fixed makeup; a mixture's makeup can vary.

topics.title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
topics.short: Particles move in every state; the states differ in how close the particles are and how freely they move.

topics.title: Physical and Chemical Changes
topics.short: A chemical change makes new substances; a physical change only changes form or state.

topics.title: SI Units and Metric Prefixes
topics.short: Each prefix is a power of ten: 1 km = 10³ m and 1 mg = 10⁻³ g.

topics.title: Measurements and Significant Figures
topics.short: Read an instrument to one estimated digit, then count the digits that carry meaning.

topics.title: Accuracy, Precision and Percent Error
topics.short: Accurate means close to the true value; precise means close to each other.

topics.title: Significant Figures in Calculations
topics.short: Products and quotients keep the fewest significant figures; sums and differences keep the fewest decimal places.

topics.title: Dimensional Analysis
topics.short: Multiply by conversion factors equal to 1, arranged so the units you do not want cancel.

topics.title: Density
topics.short: Density is mass per unit volume; use it to find a mass, a volume or the identity of a substance.

topics.title: Temperature Scales and Absolute Zero
topics.short: The kelvin scale starts at absolute zero: K = °C + 273.15.

topics.title: How We Learned What Atoms Are
topics.short: Dalton's atoms, Thomson's electrons and Rutherford's nucleus, each from an experiment.

topics.title: Protons, Neutrons and Electrons
topics.short: The number of protons, the atomic number, decides which element an atom is.

topics.title: Isotopes and Mass Number
topics.short: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons; mass number = protons + neutrons.

topics.title: Ions and Charge
topics.short: An atom that gains electrons becomes a negative ion; one that loses electrons becomes a positive ion.

topics.title: Average Atomic Mass
topics.short: The mass on the periodic table is the average of the isotopes' masses, weighted by how common each one is.

topics.title: Energy Levels and Shells
topics.short: Electrons fill levels of rising energy: 2, then 8, then 8 for the first 20 elements.

topics.title: Bright-Line Spectra
topics.short: An electron that drops to a lower level gives off light of one exact energy, so each element shows its own set of colors.

topics.title: Sublevels and Orbitals
topics.short: Level n has n sublevels (s, p, d, f), and each orbital in a sublevel holds at most two electrons.

topics.title: Electron Configurations
topics.short: Fill sublevels in order of energy, read straight off the blocks of the periodic table.

topics.title: Groups, Periods and Families
topics.short: Elements in a column have the same number of outer electrons and behave alike; each row starts a new shell.

topics.title: Valence Electrons and Dot Symbols
topics.short: Count the outer-shell electrons of a main-group atom from its group and draw them as dots.

topics.title: Atomic Radius
topics.short: Atoms get bigger down a group as shells are added, and smaller across a period as more protons pull on the same shell.

topics.title: Ionization Energy
topics.short: It takes more energy to remove an electron that is closer to more protons.

topics.title: Electronegativity
topics.short: Electronegativity measures how hard an atom pulls on shared electrons; it rises up and to the right.

topics.title: Predicting Ion Charges
topics.short: Main-group atoms gain or lose electrons to match the nearest noble gas.

topics.title: Ionic Bonds
